description:
As a species that has shaped the Earth, humans have transformed their environment like no other species before. With every new technology, our influence—and our responsibility for the future we are shaping—potentially grows. 

The tour Homo Futuris explores questions such as: How is technology changing what it means to be human? How does it shape the way we live together? What visions of the future guide us? And what role do WE play in all of this?

description:
The brain continuously generates, processes and transmits electrical signals that control all bodily functions and shape our perception. This brain activity can be recorded using brain-computer interfaces and visualized in real time. However, this measurement data can also be used for interactive, game-based formats.

description: In this mini-workshop, we show you how to isolate individual colonies from a bacterial culture using the 13-stroke method. Stroke by stroke, a dense micromix on the agar plate is transformed into a clean, smeared clone.

description:
The Ars Electronica Center’s media façade is more than just a brightly lit surface. With a few tricks, it becomes a democratic tool—visible, public and customizable.

In this workshop, you will “hack” our digital canvas and turn your ideas into colorful pixels using microcontrollers and code. Instead of spray cans, you will use the façade’s LEDs to project your messages into the urban space. description:

Separated by the BioLab, an enclosed laboratory space connected through tubes and tools, they carry out a ritualized workflow: microbial probes are prepared, biopolymers produced and microbial explorers placed into cryogenic hibernation.

title: Sonic Saturday: Audible Futures, Silent Decisions
description:
Since 2016, Anton Bruckner University (ABU) has been hosting the Sonic Saturday as part of the Ars Electronica Festival. The event features spatial sound concerts, live performances, and audiovisual and sound installations. We aim to bring together artists, researchers and an audience interested in electroacoustic music, sonic art, spatial audio and multimedia practices to allow for an informal, in-person exchange of ideas.

description:

Visitors will have the opportunity to explore experimental musical interfaces, interactive instruments and current research projects. If you are interested in visiting us, we will prepare some demos, snacks and drinks on Saturday, September 12th from 11:00 until 14:00 at the Tangible Music Lab location at the Tabakfabrik Linz.

description:

description:
Installed in the garden of the Anton Bruckner University, the DodekaOTTO Listening Experience invites visitors to encounter spatial music in an open-air setting. This unique 20-channel sound sculpture, developed by the Tangible Music Lab and OTTOsonics, creates an immersive listening environment that blends with the surrounding landscape.

description: Drawing upon the four compositions that form Random Check 8, the multimedia installation unfolds as a dynamic field of sound, image and bodily presence. Through choreographic actions and the energy generated by performers and audience alike, it continuously reconfigures the relationships between organic and synthetic forms, inviting participants into a process of transformation, reciprocity and emergence.

description:
UN-ORGANIC is the eighth edition of an interdisciplinary artistic project developed since 2019 by the Random Check Media Ensemble (RCME)—a collective of artists affiliated with the Eugeniusz Geppert Academy of Art and Design and the Karol Lipinski Academy of Music in Wrocław along with invited guest collaborators. The project comprises four audiovisual compositions, performative actions and an interactive multimedia installation.

title: The Syntax of Nature and Other Approximate Truths
description: The Syntax of Nature and Other Approximate Truths questions the status of truths commonly regarded as natural and universal. In a world increasingly shaped by algorithms and computational models, the boundary between discovering and constructing reality becomes ever more blurred. The work oscillates between the organic and the synthetic, the human and the generated, exploring a space in which the notions of origin and originality begin to dissolve. title: UN-ORGANIC
description: The eponymous composition UN-ORGANIC unfolds as an unstable ecology of drifting filaments, luminous spores, vaporous tissues and half-formed organisms. Matter hovers between dead and alive: it breathes without permission, leaks, sends signals through membranes and withdraws into shadow. Familiar divisions between organic and inorganic, natural and artificial collapse into a speculative zone of latent life, nonhuman agencies and perception caught in the undergrowth of machines.

title: NEKRO//MAKINA
description: NEKRO//MAKINA is an audiovisual ritual in which death is no longer treated as an ending, but as a state that remains active. Sound and image are bound together within a system that persists beyond collapse, continuously shifting between control and rupture, density and erosion. A fixed audiovisual core provides structure and duration, while live electronic interventions introduce instability, friction and excess. description:
Room 301 is an immersive light and sound installation created specifically for this year’s Sonic Saturday. Delving deep into their ever-expanding collection of sound and light objects, Bengler/Geissl build a site-specific sound/light experience inviting the audience to enter a new layer of their brimming Klang-/Licht STROM universe. Surging streams of sound resonate with drones of amber light. The hiss of crystal white cuts through, hitting all senses. Step in.

description:

description:
This audiovisual performance with live music, dance, moving image and immersive audio explores the limits between body, image and sound. 
Created by the collective Lluvia de Palos after more than a decade of research, this project proposes a sensory experience that brings together music, movement and image from a non-hegemonic perspective inspired by Mesoamerican thought.

title: MEET THE ARTIST: Capital Dream
description: This is a guided tour of Capital Dream, a curated group exhibition. Rather than archiving, the exhibition constructs a perspective on media art that redefines image, experience and technology. It brings together works exploring neural networks and celestial bodies, still life and living plants, the authentic self and GPT-2, as well as tensions between the desire to create and the need for control. The tour is followed by a get-together with the WRO Art Center team and all participating artists.

title: Award Ceremony u19—create your world
description:
The Award Ceremony brings together this year’s winners of the Prix Ars Electronica in the u19—create your world category. Host Conny Lee presents the 23 projects selected by the https://ars.electronica.art/prix/en/juries/jury2026/#u19createyourworld, while the young artists receive their awards and share brief insights into the ideas behind their projects.

title: Retrotopia – Wenn Vergangenheit Zukunft bestimmt: Herausforderungen für Bildung und Demokratie
description:
This year’s Symposium Perspectives on Political Education, held as part of the Ars Electronica Festival, addresses topics such as tolerance, democratic rights and social responsibility.

Across many areas of society, we are witnessing regressive developments. Hard-won progress and rights are increasingly being called into question. title: Play the Façade
description: Ars Electronica Futurelab’s Play the Façade transforms the Ars Electronica Center into an interactive audiovisual stage within the Linz skyline. Using the local Wi-Fi, visitors can connect to the building with their own smartphones, play music and control the façade’s more than 40,000 LEDs in real time. The Ars Electronica Center thus becomes an instrument that users can play—and the city a shared, luminous creative space.

title: Luminous Patterns
description:
As part of the nextcomic festival, students from the MKD – Master School of Communication Design Linz designed the façade of the Ars Electronica Center. With the watchful gaze of large-scale eyes, pulsating data streams, and the question “Am I AI?”, they transformed the museum into an empathetic entity for one hour each evening, inviting passersby to engage with topics such as surveillance, data hunger and digital privacy.

title: Symposium Tech-Bro-Topia. A Dystopian Shift of Politics, Economics and Culture?
description: Tech billionaires like Musk or Thiel promise progress through markets and technology but their visions are anti-democratic, deeply unequal and shaped by a very specific idea of masculinity. This interdisciplinary symposium brings together international experts to ask: whose future is being promoted here and by which means? Confirmed speakers include Alison Winch, Aya Jaff and Arnaud Miranda. Featuring keynotes, Q&A, and a roundtable discussion.

For us, this anniversary is not only a cause for celebration, but also the start of something new – new ideas, new stories and new experiences. description: The media façade of the Ars Electronica Center is far more than a spectacular, glowing piece of architecture. During the workshop Hack the Façade, it becomes a democratic tool for digital participation, open to all festival visitors. On Thursday, September 10th, and Friday, September 11th, from 16:30–18:30, visitors get to program the façade’s LEDs themselves, turning their ideas into glowing pixel images with nothing more than a microcontroller and some code. description:

Under the artistic direction of Dawid Liftinger and Karin Balkenhol, six independent works for the iconic façade were created at the Walter-Lübcke-Schule in Wolfhagen, Germany.

description:
Building on the focal themes WORK ON BIODIVERSITY – Biodiversity Strategy for Eastern Linz (September 10th) and Industrial District–Port of Linz – For a Different Approach to Urban Development (September 11th), the association SCHWEMMLAND and partners present a diverse two-day program.

title: KunstUni Campus Exhibition Guided Tour
description:
Join us for a guided tour of the Art and Design University of Linz campus.
Starting at the installation in the main square, you will explore the university’s main buildings and discover over 250 artworks by students, artists and international partner universities. 

The tour begins at 17:00 at Linz’s Hauptplatz (Hauptplatz 6, Infopoint), from Wednesday to Saturday, and is available in German or English. The tour lasts about 50 minutes. Free admission.

description:
The RIECS-Concept Summit brings together experts, external associates and project partners at the mid-point of the RIECS-Concept journey to work on designing the future of citizen science infrastructure. Together, we will reflect on what has been built so far, consider what comes next and mark the transition from the first phase into the project's second and final phase.

title: LINZ AG Nachklangwolke
description:
Dance music in a style all its own. An open genre crossover of dance, dub and techno-inflected grooves, drawing on club sounds from around the world. Repetitive, hypnotic, driving—made for sweaty dancefloors and long nights.

title: ATTheENDLinz—Linzer Klangwolke 26
description: ATTheENDLinz is a poetic-musical and at the same time experimental experience that engages with the city of Linz—a sensory experience of sound, space, empathy, fear, confidence and hope. Music and performative staging are used to create a collective experience: what happens in a city when its order begins to falter? title: Welcome address
description: Sarah Kriesche, Doris Weichselbaumer and Stephan Pühringer will open this conference with introductory remarks on the project and their main questions.

title: On Broligarchy
description: In the first keynote, Aya Jaff dissects the rise of a new tech elite—founders who present themselves as rebels, but rule like kings. Drawing from her own experience in the startup world, she traces how innovation became a smokescreen for power consolidation, data extraction and economic inequality.

title: The Tech-Elite and the new Fascism
description: In the second keynote Rainer Mühlhoff will deliver an in-depth analysis of the ideologies underpinning the contemporary tech-elite, in a fireside-chat exchange with Sarah Kriesche. He will discuss the threat of a new fascism emerging from the interaction of AI-ideology and the New Right. He will also illuminate the dynamics between AI, power and inequality and their significance for the structural dynamics of contemporary capitalism.

title: The New Patriarchs of Digital Capitalism
description: In this keynote, Alison Winch delivers an analysis of the gendered and racialized power dynamics underlying the rise and rule of the tech bros of Silicon Valley. The talk offers a critique of the billionaire founders of US West Coast tech companies, addressing their collective power, influence and ideology, their group dynamics and the role they play in the wider socio-cultural and political formations of digital capitalism.

title: Roundtable Discussion
description:
All keynote speakers will join a roundtable discussion moderated by Sarah Kriesche.
There will be questions posed to the panelists, prepared by the organizers. Secondly, during the workshop, the audience can submit questions digitally (via QR-Code), some of which will be selected for the Roundtable discussion.

title: Musikmaschine in concert
description: The performance explores how traditional musical material can be transformed through interaction with the Musikmaschine. Audiences experience performers combining the machine’s mechanical sounds and melodies with live electronics, synthesizers and ambient soundscapes. Rooted in the history of music-making technologies, the project examines new forms of musical expression that connect cultural heritage with contemporary electronic performance practices.

title: MEET THE SCIENTIST: ASTER+S > ART ^ GENETICS
description: The top Spanish scientist Professor Guillermo Antiñolo Gil and some emergent interdisciplinary creative teams will inspire visitors about the present and future of genetics. The professor will explain some scientific cartographies of life: healthcare big data, gene editing, clinical bioinformatics, hereditary cancer, reproductive genomics and real-world data. And the artists will introduce how they have translated these invisible territories into artistic, critical and sensitive experiences.

title: Opening Remarks
description: Stage host Vanessa Hannesschläger opens the day with a brief introduction to the programme, its key topics and the speakers joining the first day of the Theme Symposium.

title: Democracy in the Age of Digital Polarization
description: In Isaac Asimov’s 1955 story Franchise, future America is still a democracy, but a strange one: parties and candidates campaign for office but citizens have been freed of the burden of voting. A supercomputer, gently named Multivac, can very nearly compute how every American would vote. And on the election day the machine selects the single citizen who will be the Voter of the Year. title: From Outrage to Influence: How Psychology, Creators and Platforms Shape Political Debate
description:
Why does outrage spread so easily online—and how does it turn into political influence? This conversation brings together psychological insights and a closer look at the growing influence of social media creators in shaping political debate.

title: Weaponized Information - Disinformation as a Geopolitical Tool
description:
Disinformation is no longer simply a problem of false information. It has become a tool of geopolitical influence—used to exploit existing tensions, shape public narratives and undermine trust in democratic institutions. As AI makes it easier to produce and distribute convincing content at scale, the information space itself is becoming a field of conflict.

title: National Gallery Dreaming
description: What if the National Gallery collection could dream? This Al-driven installation journeys through over 2,400 artworks, uncovering unexpected connections between paintings, artists and ideas. Shaped by visitor voices, it transforms collection data into a living map of discovery. National Gallery Dreaming is an Al-powered interactive installation that explores the hidden relationships within the National Gallery, London’s collection. title: Weaponizing Confusion
description: In this workshop, Christina Schwaha and Stefan Rathmanner from the fact-checking team of the Austria Presse Agentur (APA) discuss how various actors attempt to manipulate public opinion through disinformation on social media, and how fact-checkers themselves become targets of these actors. Using concrete examples, they highlight the methods behind various campaigns and explain what each of us can do to avoid spreading this content further.

title: Designing for Peace: Technology, Trust and the Future of How We Live Together
description:
Every day, we hear about AI getting better at doing human tasks. But are those capabilities making us humans better or worse at living together in peace?
What if we evaluated AI through a different lens: its effect on our capacity to coexist? Our ability to navigate disagreement. To live with diversity and difference. To build relationships grounded in trust, dignity and belonging.

title: Designing the Digital Public: Building Spaces for Democratic Negotiation
description:
What if we stopped asking how democracy can adapt to the digital spaces we already have—and started designing those spaces with democracy in mind?

The final session of the conference turns from diagnosis to possibility, inviting the speakers to imagine the digital institutions and public spaces of the future. title: Team Tech or Team Human?
description: While tech-billionaires publicly celebrate their ”techno-optimism” (Andreessen), they secretly prepare for the possible consequences of their disruptive actions. In face of scenarios like climate collapse or civil wars they seek safety in private luxury bunkers, space colonies or in uploading their minds to the cloud; pursuing private exit-strategies rather than using their vast resources to make the world a better place. title: Patterns of Dehumanization
description: Dehumanization rarely begins with violence. It begins with language, with images, with enemy stereotypes in everyday life. Antisemitism is one of the oldest patterns of this kind, and in the digital space it is simultaneously taking on new, accelerated forms: algorithms amplify outrage and enemy images, antisemitic narratives spread globally and instantly, old stereotypes resurface in new digital forms and threats born online increasingly spill into physical, everyday life. title: B10d13$3L-LLM as a performative installation
description: B10d13$3L-LLM is a performative installation by Gökay Atabek—developed in collaboration with Jan Zuiderveld and Ritsert Mans—that shows the often-hidden costs of Artificial Intelligence. The work uses a slow, “little language model” AI agent that runs on a single microcomputer powered by DIY biodiesel. In a darkly humorous way, it reveals the materiality, energy consumption and infrastructural limits of AI.

title: Ra Asensi’s [Meta]morphe
description: Ra Asensi’s [Meta]morphe explores transformations in postindustrial sites. Their alter ego asfàltica emerges from industrial ruins and travels through water. Aqueous and earthy, aerial and electric, hyperdense líquid-y, their performance and installation will combine electric poetry, touch and sound. The work will engage with physical, ecological and mediated aspects of the Danube.

title: The Sound of the Day: A Communal Sound Gathering with elekhlekha (อีเหละเขละขละ)
description: In this performance, elekhlekha (อีเหละเขละขละ) invites audiences to a communal participatory sound-making, activating their Network Gong Ensemble Archive—an interactive website, homemade gongs and found objects. Rooted in Southeast Asian oral and musical traditions threatened by displacement, the project asks whether sound and story can be archived without losing their living, relational meaning. Visitors of all ages are welcome to play, listen and add their own voice to the ensemble.

title: Test_Lab: Incompleteness as Reorientation
description: A live event with the artists Sondi, Ra Asensi and Gokay Atabek , as well as V2_’s Boris Debackere and Florian Weigl. Test_Lab: Incompleteness as Reorientation is part of V2_’s public event series that offers an informal space for presenting, testing and discussing artistic research and development.

title: EMAP Get Together
description: The European Media Art Platform EMAP Extended invites artists, curators and partners to a Get Together. The event brings together members of the 16-organization consortium behind EMAP’s residency program, and offers an opportunity to meet former and current artists in residence as well as partners and to discuss developments in the fields of media art, bioart and robotic art across Europe.

title: Negotiating with Water
description:
Negotiating with Water is a conference programme dedicated to our water imaginaries, and their legal and geopolitical realities and possibilities. The day frames water as a symptom of the socio-political context and a witness to different forms of human activities. Through the gaze of capital, water is a resource, a commodity we negotiate the rights to; at the same time, water carries traces of military, logistic or commercial activity.

description: Curator Ana-Maria Carabelea gives a brief introduction to the topic and the day's program.

title: Water through a Legal Lens: From Private Commodity to the Heritage of Mankind
description:
Stefano Burchi's talk unpacks the evolving legal conceptions of (fresh)water, from water as a private commodity to water as public property regulated by nation-states through national water laws, all the way to the water of boundary rivers, lakes and aquifers framed in treaties and agreements between multiple nation-states. These legal conceptions illustrate how nation-states and, more broadly, humans and societies relate to water.

title: Art for the Hydrocommons
description: The hydrocommons is the complex set of connections and permeations between human and non-human bodies of water. It does away with the illusory separation between the two and invites a reimaging of their relations outside capitalist or colonial frames that, in attempts to master, manage, engineer and contain this force of nature, position humanity in opposition to it. title: The Flows of Law, Technology and Empire Through Water and History
description: The lecture will highlight how the entwinement of law and technology in the imperialist project plays out across bodies of water. Drawing on examples from different regions across the world, the lecture will provide insights into how colonialism and neocolonialism use law and technology as distinct techniques for the control and domination of waters and peoples.

title: Fluid Media
description: Water both sustains life on the planet and threatens it by exceeding human control. These contradictory perceptions produce different relations to aquatic environments. description: There is a worm in our robot! At least its brain—because a worm’s nervous system can already be “copied” into a machine. But even the human brain, with all the data it produces, can already be read and interpreted well by using EEG and brain/computer interfaces, and can even control things outside the body.

title: Town Hall Meeting: ArtScience X ArsBiologica
description: What actually happens in the space between an artist and a scientist? Beyond what gets produced, how does the encounter change both sides? This session explores how bringing artistic and scientific methodologies into genuine dialogue can transform public engagement, reframe scientific inquiry and seed long-term ecological awareness. This Town Hall meeting builds on the Ars Biologica residencies of the České Budějovice – European Capital of Culture 2028 and its partners Ars Electronica’s and TBA2

description:
What practices help us collaborate when uncertainty, complexity and diverse perspectives become the norm? 
Feminist Tools for the Future is an open gathering for researchers, artists, designers, technologists and practitioners of all genders and fields to exchange experiences, share methods that work, and build new connections across disciplines. description: Ever wondered how to partner with the Ars Electronica Festival?At this open networking session, you’ll meet the people behind the festival and hear first-hand how collaborations take shape. description: How to collaborate with Prix Ars Electronica? Would you like to host an exhibition of award-winning works in your city? Invite award winners to conduct workshops? Apply insights from the winning works to your own field of expertise? Or use past works from the Ars Electronica Archive for educational purposes? Ars Electronica staff will answer your questions about the various collaboration opportunities with Prix Ars Electronica. Let’s discuss the possibilities for the future.

description: In recent years, hundreds of citizen science projects have proven capable of delivering top quality research. There is now a real opportunity, and a pressing need, to build a dedicated Research Infrastructure for citizen science. description: Initiated in collaboration with CARE Austria, this conference explores how Artificial Intelligence can contribute to addressing humanitarian, social, and environmental challenges. Drawing on her artistic and theoretical practice, she examines the shifting relationships between technology, power, human experience and collective agency. title: One in seven: Austria 1946, Uganda 2026—who gets to be a person in a crisis?
description:
Not all crises are seen equally—and neither are the people living through them. This keynote explores how visibility, data and global attention shape our understanding of humanitarian crises and asks what this means as Artificial Intelligence becomes increasingly influential in humanitarian and social impact work.

Beginning with the history of the CARE Package in post-war Austria, the keynote connects past and present experiences of crisis and reflects on the agency of those affected. Drawing o

title: Who Shapes the Future?
description:
Who gets to shape the future of Artificial Intelligence—and whose voices risk being left out?

Bringing together perspectives from technology and humanitarian practice, this conversation explores how AI can be developed in ways that are equitable, inclusive and accountable. Archana Prasad, founder of http://gooey.ai/, brings the perspective of a technologist and entrepreneur working at the intersection of AI and social impact, while Jerry Tuan, CEO of CARE USA, contributes insights from global h

title: AI for Social Impact Award: Insights from the Jury & Introduction to the Initiative
description:
How can Artificial Intelligence contribute to meaningful social change—and what does it take for an AI-driven project to create impact that is not only innovative, but also responsible, inclusive and sustainable?

This session introduces the AI for Social Impact Award, its vision, objectives and selection process. The award seeks to recognize initiatives that use AI to address pressing social and humanitarian challenges while placing people, communities and ethical responsibility at the center o

title: AI for Social Impact Award: The award winning projects
description:
What does it look like when Artificial Intelligence is designed not simply to innovate, but to respond to real social and humanitarian needs?

This session presents the five winning initiatives of the AI for Social Impact Initiative, showcasing projects that combine technological innovation with measurable social impact, ethical design and meaningful engagement with the communities they aim to serve. Spanning education, agriculture, historical justice, migrant health and maternal care, the proje

title: Negotiating Humanity
description:
Bringing the symposium to a close, this panel explores what it means to keep humanity at the center of Artificial Intelligence in humanitarian action. It brings together perspectives from AI innovation, humanitarian practice, critical data studies and community-centered implementation to examine both the potential and the tensions that arise when AI is developed and deployed in contexts of vulnerability and crisis.

The discussion features Eniola Benson and Shadi Henchiri, Grand Prize winners of

title: From AI for Good to AI for Action
description: The closing remarks summarize the key insights of the symposium and emphasize the transition from dialogue to implementation. Andrea Barschdorf-Hager highlights the shared responsibility of institutions, technology developers, artists, humanitarian organizations and communities to transform principles into concrete action and sustained collaboration.

title: Contested Futures – Europe Negotiating Power, Machine, Labour
description:
If being human has always been a process of negotiation, then this day asks the following question: How does Europe negotiate its future, when so much of that future is now built into the machines, the infrastructures of modern power, underpinning our collective life?

It is not a settled question. It is not a friendly one. The same drive for digital sovereignty can also build public infrastructure held in common—or a militarized arsenal dressed in the aesthetics of a new authoritarianism. The f

title: Ars Electronica Campus Award Ceremony
description:
The third edition of the Ars Electronica Campus Award aims to recognize the most outstanding project presented within this year’s Ars Electronica Campus Exhibition, which highlights not only emerging talents but also the educational institutions that support them. A jury formed of three renowned experts in the field of media arts will inspect the projects and select five Honorary Mentions and one Grand Prize, which includes €2.000 in prize money.

The Ars Electronica Campus Exhibition is a joint

title: Networking Event Gwangyang – Linz Media Arts Exchange 2026
description: This networking event introduces the third edition of the Gwangyang—Linz Media Arts Exchange, an initiative dedicated to artistic collaboration and knowledge sharing between South Korea and Austria. Meet the curators and artists of this program and be part when Korean artist Soh Boram and Austrian artist Heike Waldner-Kaltenbrunner will each receive the grant to exhibit their work in Gwangyang and Linz. The event is open to artists, curators and festival visitors interested in international coll

title: Artists’ Reception hosted by the Slovenian Embassy in Austria
description:
Ars Electronica Festival, the Slovenian Embassy in Austria, the Slovenian Cultural and Information Centre SKICA Wien and the Municipality of Celje warmly invite artists, curators and culture practicioners to join us for the Artists’ Reception—an opportunity to mingle, connect and exchange with fellow professionals from the field of media arts.

The event will also celebrate the Slovenian artist Robertina Šebjanič who has received an Award of Distinction in the category Interactive Art+ of the Pr

title: Where Is the Sound Hiding?
description:
The C. Bechstein Centrum Linz invites children on a journey into the world of pianos, full of opportunities to discover, explore and try things out for themselves.
What does the sound of a piano string have in common with the beating wings of a bee? And how many elephants would it take to create the right tension for a piano string? Through playful experiments, children learn how a piece of wood becomes a musical instrument, how piano strings are wound and how sound is ultimately created inside

title: Creative Europe Get Together
description: Ars Electronica and Creative Europe Desk Austria will once again be hosting the Creative Europe Get Together, an event that brings together European partners from across a variety of sectors in a friendly environment, where attendees can meet and share perspectives. As the EU’s flagship program supporting the cultural, creative and audiovisual sectors, Creative Europe has promoted numerous meaningful programs, such as MEDIA, with a focus on the film industry—and this year we will be celebrating

title: Networking Event hosted by the Creative Industries Fund NL
description:
The Creative Industries Fund NL, CIIIC and Ars Electronica Festival warmly invite you to this networking gathering, where you will have the opportunity to get to know more about five consortia dedicated to artistic and design research for immersive experiences consisting of makers, producers, cultural institutions and researchers.

This event will offer a closer look at the ongoing multi-annual activity programmes of the consortia, while creating space to meet potential European partners working

title: Reality Screenshot
description: Reality Screenshot is a hybrid performance based on [ The Frame ], reinterpreted through Domestic Data Streamers’ data visualization approach. The event presents a “Human Artificial Intelligence” made of flesh and bones, which observes and interprets everyday habits, curiosities and social tensions in public space. Blending street theater and data visualization, it invites audiences to reflect on perception while turning the city into a living stage for emotion, participation and discovery.

title: The Next Chapter: Lessons Learned and Futures Beyond S+T+ARTS
description:
This year marks the conclusion of the European Commission’s STARTS (Science, Technology and the Arts) initiative, a key pillar of European innovation policy for the past decade. Through hundreds of residencies and cross-sector collaborations, STARTS has demonstrated the value of bringing artists, scientists, technologists, industry and cultural institutions together to tackle complex societal challenges.

Following the launch of the Science + Technology + Arts: Lessons Learned from a Decade of T

title: Never In Our Image – Gun Destruction Opera
description: As part of STWST84x12 HAUNTED, one act of the three-part Queer Gun Destruction Opera Never In Our Image will be performed. Here, weapons are sawed apart, cut up and melted down. Instruments are then cast from these destroyed weapons, sound sculptures are created as part of a process of reclaiming weapons and musical scores are composed. Through the transformation of metal and sound, as well as the staging with a queer community, the fundamental question is posed: What if metal never wanted to be

title: Expert Tour Negotiating Beyond Humanity: Masha Zolotova (EN)
description: As the Ars Electronica Festival 2026 explores new ways of negotiating our place in an interconnected world, the Negotiating Beyond Humanity exhibition invites us to shift our attention beyond the human. Together with Masha Zolotova, co-curator of this exhibition, we embark on a journey of discovery: How can artistic practices help us attune to more-than-human perspectives and rethink coexistence, care and agency through encounters with diverse forms of life, knowledge and sensory experiences?

title: Urban Metamorphosis. Sketches of Tomorrow.
description:
The project explores how climate adaptation can transform existing urban spaces into places that support human well-being, biodiversity and a higher quality of life. It shows how cities can be reimagined when climate action is understood not as a limitation, but as an opportunity for creating more vibrant and resilient environments.

Selected public spaces were captured with a 360-degree 3D camera to preserve their unique characteristics.  These real places were transformed through 3D modelling,

title: Keys Beyond Boundaries
description:
Electronics meets improvised piano; dance, film, poetry and more.
From the performative film El Cultivo de la Mente with live piano accompaniment to the Linz-based electronic music acts The Unsettled and Tomá Ivanov, this year’s program at the C. Bechstein Piano Centrum Linz brings together a wide range of artistic expressions. Live improvised piano serves as the common thread, merging film, dance, spoken word, electronic music, contemporary soundscapes and immersive audiovisual experiences.

title: Minimal Music Highlights by Maki Namekawa
description: Maki Namekawa is one of the leading pianists of our time. The Japanese artist has earned an international reputation for her outstanding interpretations of both the classical and contemporary repertoire. She has enjoyed a particularly close relationship with the Ars Electronica Festival in Linz for many years, where she regularly appears with innovative programs and interdisciplinary projects. At the C. Bechstein Centrum Linz, Maki Namekawa will perform in two concerts. While celebrated as a cla

title: Minute Paintings / Pictures of an Exhibition
description: At the beginning of Minute Paintings / Pictures of an Exhibition, users encounter seven blank, framed canvases presented in the Petersburg style on the wall, which they can paint one after the other using various techniques. These techniques are inspired by the works of different artists. Users can create two painted versions of each canvas and then choose the more interesting one. The finished exhibition can be saved, and users can also view the most recently created exhibitions in a slideshow.

title: Deep Space Selection
description: At Deep Space Selection, we present several times a day a changing selection from our diverse program, which we’ve been continuously developing since 2009. Visitors can look forward to exciting stories and immersive experiences spanning media art, science and technology.

title: Unbreakable Ukraine
description:
Unbreakable Ukraine is an immersive exhibition born to safeguard Ukraine’s cultural heritage, now under constant threat from war.
Through high-resolution 3D scans, cinematic animation and emotional spatial storytelling, visitors are brought into direct encounter with some of Ukraine’s most significant landmarks—Saint Sophia in Kyiv, Saint George in Lviv, the Library of Chernihiv, the Opera House of Odesa, Karazin University in Kharkiv—sites scarred by conflict and under serious threat, documente

title: Lost Legends
description: Life on Earth has produced an astonishing diversity of creatures, each adapted to its own place and time. Many of these remarkable animals have vanished, leaving behind only fossils, preserved specimens and fragments of evidence. Using highly detailed 3D models created from fossils and extant specimens in the collections of the Natural History Museum Vienna, this experience combines scientific evidence with immersive visualization to bring these lost legends back to life. This journey follows th

title: Laguna Obscura
description:
Inspired by the magic lantern and phantasmagoria, Laguna Obscura explores the origins of immersion within the Venetian imaginary.  
Turning the lagoon into a symbolic membrane, the work unfolds as a living archive where archival fragments emerge as fleeting illusions suspended between presence and absence. Laguna Obscura reactivates historical traces as hauntological presences, exploring immersion as a threshold where memory, vision and imagination converge.

title: A Sky of Infinite Wishes
description: This is the world premiere of the newest artwork from Sputniko!, commissioned by Julius Baer Bank in collaboration with Ars Electronica. In this installation, an evolving panoramic dusk sky overflows with signs and symbols of good fortune drawn from East Asian tradition, inviting us to question the dissolving boundary between authenticity and fabrication in an age of AI-generated worlds.

title: Next Singularity, the Intelligence of Life
description: For nearly 50 years, artist Yoichiro Kawaguchi has utilized his original “Growth Model” to explore biological forms and evolution through computer-generated art, blending natural mathematics with advanced technology. His work, drawing inspiration from the Cambrian explosion, argues that AI should be a creative partner for discovering human singularity rather than a tool for producing standardized, mediocre content.

title: MERGING VISIONS
description: MERGING VISIONS is an immersive experience that expands the urban digital twin into a medium for storytelling and worldbuilding, exploring the Salzburg Festival site. Through three chapters, visitors journey across scales and time, exploring the site’s geological, cultural and ecological dimensions. Layered visualizations bring ecological processes, more-than-human relationships and intangible cultural qualities into urban representation.

title: Quantum Zoom – The First Chapter
description: Quantum Zoom is a 3D stereoscopic immersive experience developed for Deep Space 8K in cooperation with Ars Electronica, DESY, BOKU University and IQOQI Vienna, where audiences will step into a vast, evolving system of nested realities. As they move deeper—from the visible world into microscopic and quantum domains—they will witness the flow of information as it self-organizes into different structures of reality. This culminates in a revelation: the entire system operates like a living quantum s

title: A Quarter Century of Processing
description: Processing turns 25 this year. Join us to celebrate the past, present and future of Processing—as software, design philosophy, pedagogical approach and global creative community. Reflect on a quarter century of open-source innovation and discover how Processing has empowered a generation of artists, educators and tool builders, while continuing to shape new forms of creative expression, learning and technological experimentations.

title: Perpetual Records
description: Perpetual Records is a large-scale immersive experience that invites audiences into a poetic dimension inspired by the Akashic Records—a metaphysical archive of all human experiences. Through generative visuals and sacred geometry patterns created with facial data, the work explores themes of collective consciousness. The screening offers a cinematic journey into crystalline fractal worlds, reflecting on how technology can foster self‑awareness in an increasingly fragmented world.

title: The Last Judgement Triptych by Hieronymus Bosch
description:
Hieronymus Bosch’s The Last Judgement Triptych is one of the most prominent works in the Paintings Gallery of Vienna’s Academy and is part of Austria’s cultural heritage. Its bizarre visual world, populated by devils and demons, offers insight into late medieval thought and has lost none of its fascination to this day.
The religious imagery serves as a moral admonition and includes depictions of the Last Judgment with the canon of the Seven Deadly Sins, scenes from the story of Creation and Hell

title: Interactive Brosch – Red Dinosaurs
description: This event explores how Klemens Brosch’s unfinished late work Red Dinosaurs can be reinterpreted and recontextualized through new technologies. Visitors encounter a gigapixel reproduction of the painting, an abstract animation and an interactive installation based on the artwork. The project investigates how art archives can become living spaces for dialogue, bringing historical works back into public discourse and creating new connections between cultural heritage and contemporary society.

title: Agentic Systems in Immersive Spaces
description: What if Deep Space could do more than simply display content—what if it could perceive what is happening within it and respond? In Agentic Systems in Immersive Spaces, an AI-based agent system becomes a partner to both guide and audience. As the guide tells stories, provides context, and leads visitors through projects by Ars Electronica Solutions, the agent responds to questions and situations, retrieves content, and makes unexpected connections. The presentation thus becomes a dialogue between

title: Deep Space Community
description:
What began in Linz now connects Deep Space locations in more than eight countries across three continents. In this session, partners from the international network take the audience on a journey through their spaces. In a series of concise insights, they present new openings, applications, stories, and performances—from interactive science communication to artistic and nature-based experiences.
Every Deep Space is unique, shaped by its local context, its audience, and the creative vision of the

title: [not] breaking the cycle
description: An exploration of the way we move through different cyclical phases, from order to chaos back to order again. Trying to find the answers to questions, such as: How do things interact when they attract? How can our perceptions be distorted and how do they change upon observation? In finding answers, we return to the start—learning from scratch. Ultimately, the point is not to break the cycle, but find movements with(in) it.

title: Inner Radiance
description: How can we perceive worlds lying hidden within us, and how can excavating the unseen of the human organism help us better internalize our commonalities? This is investigated here via live ultrasound—generating 3D volumes of dancers whose interiors expand into the immersive environment of Deep Space; choreographically performing within their interior selves—representationally and abstractly—to engage with medical technology beyond its diagnostic contexts and surface visual biases.

title: Samsara of Blossom: Resonance
description: Samsara of Blossom: Resonance explores how movement rooted in Korean traditional dance can be reimagined through media art. In the first collaboration between Jajack Movement and media artists Razieh Kooshki & Vahid Qaderi, performers interact with an evolving visual landscape that responds to breath, rhythm and motion. The work connects Korean cultural heritage with contemporary digital practice, revealing new forms of resonance between body, technology and perception.

title: Live-programming Deep Space 8K with vvvv
description: vvvv is a visual live-programming environment suited to large-scale interactive installations, making it ideal for Ars Electronica’s Deep Space 8K, with its dual 16×9 metre stereoscopic screens, real-time floor tracking and immersive potential. This session demonstrates live-programming Deep Space 8K through demos exploring key features of vvvv and the space, offering artists a starting point for developing their own interactive works.

title: Onassis ONX Showcase
description: Onassis ONX presents a selection of four moving image works including Explorers by Gabriel Barcia-Colombo, INTERSTITIAL MAINTENANCE by Peter Burr, Wahoo Blast by Eirini Linardaki and Forager: Spore to Forest Floor by Winslow Porter and Elie Zananiri. Spanning video, game engine renderings and textile-based digital landscapes, the program reflects on community, ecology, the residue of procedural worlds and other systems shaping contemporary life.

title: Faust 2023 revised
description: In 2023, to mark Max Reinhardt’s 150th birthday, the Ars Electronica Futurelab—in collaboration with the Salzburg Festival—virtually reconstructed Clemens Holzmeister’s monumental “Faust City” from Reinhardt’s legendary production of Faust (1933). Using materials from the Festival archive, Faust VR was then created . In 2026, a revised version of the Virtual Reality experience will be presented at the X-Reality-Lab in Salzburg, supplemented by insights into its creation at Deep Space 8K.

title: Artist Walk Tour: Negotiating Humanity
description:
Join us for a special guided tour led by Emiko Ogawa, Head of the Prix Ars Electronica. Together with the award recipients, she will lead visitors through the Prize Winners Exhibition, offering exclusive insights into the featured works.
Experience the award-winning projects of the Prix Ars Electronica and the S+T+ARTS Prize in the company of the artists themselves. Through brief artist talks and informal conversations, you will gain a deeper understanding of their ideas, backgrounds and artisti

title: Prix Ars Electronica Insight
description:
This program brings together six works that capture the spirit of this year’s Prix Ars Electronica jury discussions. Five of them received awards, standing out for their artistic intelligence, critical insight and political urgency.
The program opens with two works that place dialogue at their center. Exhibition³ is an anaglyphic 3D animation in which painter Sabine Hertig and animation artist Dirk Koy engage in an artistic dialogue within a virtual exhibition space, exploring new possibilities

title: Why The Met Is Advancing Cultural Heritage Digitization: A Spotlight on Its Collaboration with Japan’s NHK
description: In this presentation The Metropolitan Museum of Art (The Met) and the Japanese Public Broadcaster NHK will discuss the future of digital cultural heritage. The Met will introduce the 120-year history of its Imaging Department, as well as new initiatives around 3D scanning, and Augmented Reality/Virtual Reality. The Met and NHK will then focus in detail on a recent collaborative digitization project of key collection highlights, and the possibilities unlocked by the two teams coming together.

title: Tell Me About It
description:
Since 2017, Time’s Up has been researching, developing and building Turnton2047, bringing it to life through immersive environments. At its heart is a transformed economy that prioritizes the wellbeing of people and the planet while challenging existing concentrations of wealth and power. It also explores the potential of marine regeneration to restore damaged ecosystems.
Developed in collaboration with Theater Phönix, this immersive audio experience invites audiences into the everyday lives of

title: Dissonant Stereoscopy
description: Alisa Martynova’s residency at the Ars Electronica Futurelab in 2026 explores perception, consciousness and the unstable nature of truth through an immersive projection environment developed for Deep Space 8K. Drawing from studies on binocular rivalry, entropy and the default neural network, this work examines how the brain constructs reality from fragmented and ambiguous visual information. Dissonant Stereoscopy places the audience within sensory thresholds where the visual system attempts to d

title: Playtime
description: Students enrolled in the degree program Time-based and Interactive Media Art at the University of Arts Linz have developed interactive games tailored specifically to the needs and interests of our youngest visitors. Colorful, action-packed and super fun—here, children can actively engage in imaginative worlds and experience digital technologies in a playful way.

title: Ars Electronica Solutions Tour (EN)
description: During this tour of the Ars Electronica Solutions showcase, we offer personal insights into our ways of working and the development of the exhibition. We show how innovative concepts emerge from initial ideas, questions and technological possibilities and how they are transformed into immersive experiences through creative processes, interdisciplinary collaboration and the use of cutting-edge technologies. Visitors will discover how content, data and complex interrelationships can become interac

title: Hello Words! Behind the Prototype: How Ideas Become Experiences
description:
From the first concepts and prototypes to exhibition architecture and visitor experiences, explore how ideas are tested, iterated and transformed into something people can experience—and contribute to.

Following selected Hello Worlds! tours, meet the people behind the prototypes and artworks and gain an inside look at what usually remains invisible: the research, experiments, technologies, design decisions and collaborative processes behind the works. This is your opportunity to ask questions a

title: Hello Worlds! Behind the Artworks:  No Bird & Algorithms in Reflection
description: Following selected Hello Worlds! tours, meet the artists behind No Bird and Algorithms in Reflection. Gain an inside look at the ideas, artistic research, experiments and design decisions behind the works, and explore how they reflect on coexistence, shared habitats, ecological change and life in a world shared by humans, other species and increasingly autonomous technologies. No slides—just artworks, people and conversation.

title: Hello Worlds! Behind the Prototype / Artwork: Deep Mirror & Algorithms in Reflection
description:
Explore how AI interprets people, and how those interpretations shape the way we understand ourselves.

Following selected Hello Worlds! tours, meet the people behind the prototypes and artworks and gain an inside look at what usually remains invisible: the research, experiments, technologies, design decisions and collaborative processes behind the works. This is your opportunity to ask questions and talk directly with the researchers, artists, designers, and developers.

title: Hello Worlds! Behind the Prototype: Amplify Me – Visions
description: What happens when technologies no longer stay in our pockets, but become part of our bodies, clothes, and everyday lives? Discover how Amplify Me – Visions combines speculative concepts with experimental prototypes to explore mobility, human augmentation, and what we might become. Developed together with Toyota Motor Corporation’s Advanced Design Division, these visions draw on expertise in automotive UX and industrial design to imagine new relationships between people, technology and movement.

title: Hello Worlds! Behind the Prototype: Hello Worlds! System
description:
Whether you're curious about the technology, the research, the design process, or the collaboration itself—ask us anything.
Following selected Hello Worlds! tours, meet the people behind the prototype and get an inside look at what usually remains invisible: the research, experiments, technologies, design decisions and collaborative processes that shaped the experience at the Ars Electronica Center. No slides—just prototypes, people and conversation.

title: Hello Worlds! Behind the Prototype: Hybrid Thinking
description:
Explore if AI can help us think rather than simply providing answers with Futurelab’s Hybrid Thinking prototype in the Hello Worlds! exhibition.

Following selected Hello Worlds! tours, meet the people behind the prototypes and artworks and gain an inside look at what usually remains invisible: the research, experiments, technologies, design decisions and collaborative processes behind the works. This is your opportunity to ask questions and talk directly with the researchers, artists, designers

title: Hello Worlds! Behind the Prototype: Interbeing Lab (Corpus Corax & Conversations Beyond the Ordinary)
description: Why do we try to talk to everyday objects—and why do we seek conversations with AI and ravens? Following selected Hello Worlds! tours, meet the people responsible for the prototypes and explore the research, technologies and design decisions behind the works. Ask questions and talk directly with the researchers, artists, designers and developers. No slides—just prototypes, people and conversation.

title: Hello Worlds! Behind the Prototype: Resonance Loom
description:
What do weaving and AI have in common? Meet the team behind the Resonance Loom and discuss how textile traditions, digital fabrication, human resonance and generative AI share a common language of patterns, instructions and algorithms. Through demonstrations and conversation, discover how centuries-old craft continues to inspire AI—and how AI, in turn, opens up new possibilities for textile thinking and crafting resonance.

Following selected Hello Worlds! tours, meet the people behind the proto

title: Hello Worlds! Futurelab Tour (EN)
description:
Explore Hello Worlds! together with the people behind the project. Researchers, artists, designers, developers, and collaboration partners guide you through the exhibition, sharing the ideas, technologies and research behind the works—and, if you like, continue the conversation afterwards.

Hello Worlds! is the public outcome of the Future Humanity Project, an experimental research collaboration between Ars Electronica Futurelab and Toyota Motor Corporation’s Advanced R&D and Engineering Company

title: Agentic Systems as a New Form of Dialogue
description: Agentic systems can be much more than mere information providers: they engage in dialogue with people, respond to individual interests and at the same time draw attention to topics and realms of knowledge that may not yet be visible within a particular context. Using the agentic systems in the Ars Electronica Solutions showcase as an example, we explore how new interfaces, the visualization of digital agents and lifelike forms of communication create a dynamic, dialogical approach to knowledge—a

title: MEET THE ARTIST: Plant Blindness
description: This presentation explores how technology shapes perception of urban nature. Reimagining certain Hong Kong flowers, such as frangipani, jacaranda and purple azalea, through immersive algorithmic visuals, it introduces evolving digital ecosystems between organic growth and digital permanence. Rooted in Hong Kong’s dense urban ecology, the artists offer global audiences new perspectives on biodiversity, environmental awareness and how art and technology can deepen attention to overlooked nature in

title: Empathetic Interfaces and New Forms of Knowledge Transfer
description: How can interfaces and interaction models be designed to make knowledge not only accessible, but also emotionally and sensorially tangible? This deep dive offers insights into the development process—from initial concept and the design of communication channels and interactions to technical implementation. Using the Ars Electronica Solutions – A Glimpse Behind the Scenes as an example, it demonstrates how empathic technologies emerge and how innovative forms of communication can open up new ways

title: Hello Worlds! Futurelab Tour (DE)
description:
Hello Worlds! is a new exhibition at the Ars Electronica Center and the public outcome of the Future Humanity Project, an experimental research collaboration between Ars Electronica Futurelab and Toyota Motor Corporation’s Advanced R&D and Engineering Company.
Hello Worlds! is an open platform where artistic prototypes, interactive installations and visitor participation become part of an ongoing exploration of what it means to be human in an age of embodied AI.

title: Ghost Stories: Negotiating Between Worlds
description: When we negotiate, we keep spaces open rather than close them through certainty or persuasion. We resist closure and remain with ambiguity. We dwell on the threshold. In such in-between spaces, where what is at stake refuses to be settled, ghosts appear. They return because something remains unresolved. They carry memories, histories and desires that continue to seek recognition. They animate absences and make visible what usually escapes perception. They inhabit thresholds where categories blur

title: Young Animations
description:
As part of the Prix Animation Art Screening, Young Animations presents a selection of short films by young artists up to age of 19 that were submitted to the Prix Ars Electronica in the u19—create your world category and to the <19 Shape your world! competition organized by our Hungarian partner organization C3.

The film program will be presented at medSPACE on the MED Campus, alongside other films selected for the https://ars.electronica.art/negotiatinghumanity/en/view/PrixArsElectronicaAnimat

title: Practicing Impact: When Reality Talks Back
description: The Ars Electronica Futurelab explores the future by building it—together with companies, institutions, researchers, artists, designers and the public. This Town Hall brings together collaborators who turn ideas into reality. When existing formats no longer fit, we invent new ones. Rather than presenting success stories, we share the realities of experimentation, negotiation and practice—because impact is not an idea. It is something you create by doing.

title: SynTact: Guided Exploration & Discussion
description: SynTact explores how future teams might extend beyond humans to include plants, robotic systems, and other forms of intelligence and life. Through touch as a shared mode of communication, the installation investigates new forms of more-than-human collaboration. This Guided Exploration invites visitors to experience SynTact together with artists and researchers, combining a live interaction with the installation and an open discussion around the ideas, questions, and processes behind the work.

title: Austrian Panorama
description:
Austrian Panorama presents a selection of the most compelling Austrian works submitted to the Prix Ars Electronica 2026 in the New Animation Art category. Following the screening, participating filmmakers and artists will join the audience for a Q&A to discuss their works and creative processes.

mouse.mp4, Jana Welte (AT), Laura-Christina Palmetshofer (AT), Pia Putz (AT), Rosa Ressi & Ramona Kranzl (AT), 8:52 min
Mouse.mp4 is a hybrid short film exploring the meaninglessness of existence in dig

title: Who Decides the Music?
description: This workshop asks who decides the music when machines generate endless sound on demand, which is as much a cultural question as it is an artistic one. Participants read a scene to music and then hear that same moment take on three different directions by using Soundbook, a tool built by Mathis Nitschke’s EU co-funded CORPUS project at Sofilab. He then demonstrates how contributing musicians actually co-own this corpus of music as opposed to simply supplying it. Filmmakers, game designers and mu

title: Basic Income for Artists – Ireland as a Model
description: After a successful pilot program, Ireland has implemented a Universal Basic Income (UBI) for artists. This basic security allows creators to work with greater freedom and independence from commercial considerations. Featuring firsthand insights from Ireland, this session will discuss how to build on the experience. Then, after a brief introduction to UBI in general, it will take a look at the economic conditions of artists in Austria and open the floor to an audience discussion.

title: A Furry Engineer!
description: What can we learn from the transformative powers of the beaver? In this workshop, participants will experiment with creative futuring and forecasting methods to generate nuanced, multi-species scenarios that reframe the beaver from a passive wild animal to an active, technical and cultural stakeholder in landscape design and restoration. A guided process will unleash their imagination to co-create speculative worlds, culminating in a historical, yet tangible retrospective from the year 2051.

title: Media Art Practice: collaborate, conserve, context and intentionality
description: This event by NEWART foundation, in collaboration with Encyclopedia of New Media Art, Volume II, Artist and Practice editor Paul Thomas, will create a documented alternative discussion focusing on artists' perspective on the sustainability of media art practice. To achieve this, we have invited five significant artists to facilitate discussion new media projects. This short provocation is presented to help create a dynamic community discussion with the goal of generating ideas for sustainable me

title: Olfactory Biome: The Smell is the Message!
description:
Create your own fragrance for the Olfactory Biome installation by using pheromone-like compounds and scent molecules that function as either attractants or repellents. By combining scents that subtly convey social signals, you can produce olfactory messages that express both yourself and your current mood.

After blending your fragrance for the first 30 minutes, you will then be guided through the olfactory installation. Experience how invisible chemical signals shape our social interactions, pe

title: Soiled
description: Is soil alive? Investigating this seemingly simple question, this workshop will enable participants to discover life in the dark ground below. Evolving from scientists who experimentally search for signs of life in soil, participants will embody various forms of soiled life and artistically express their present and immanent reality. Bridging these worlds, the workshop will provide scientific and creative materials so that the complex relevance of soil can be encountered from individual angles.

title: The Virus Stories We Carry
description: What if we could meet viruses on a human scale? This hands-on workshop invites participants to encounter viruses through touch, embodiment and collective making. Participants exchange virus stories, engage with materials from contemporary virology and create life-sized virus forms. Through artistic exploration and dialogue, they reflect on their relationships with viruses, urban ecologies and shared futures. Each participant leaves with a photographic portrait of their handmade virus.

title: Whose Future Are You Building?
description: The workshop asks what futures your project helps to build—and whose values, needs and agency it supports. TAH brings together Technology, Arts and Humanities: systems and feasibility, imagination and experience, values and social context. Using the AI-enabled TAH Prism, prompt cards and a visual canvas, participants uncover blind spots, reframe one real project, identify a responsible next step and gain a reusable transdisciplinary method developed within the Erasmus+ TransInnovate project.

title: Water Whisperer
description: Water Whisperer is an immersive participatory AI installation where visitors converse with the Danube, rain, snow, fog, groundwater and wastewater as living voices with their own interests played by AI agents. Rather than acting as an answer machine, AI facilitates collective dialogue, encouraging participants to negotiate different ecological perspectives and recognize themselves not as managers of water, but as part of an interconnected water cycle.

title: Expert Tour: Meet the Features Partners
description: The Ars Electronica Features Exhibition showcases a carefully curated selection of international projects at the intersection of art and technology. Sixteen partners explore what it means to act, decide and make meaning at a moment when the boundaries between human intention, algorithmic process and biological life have become difficult to locate. Christl Baur, Head of the Ars Electronica Festival and Program Director, provides an insight into the collaborations behind the exhibition and introdu

title: Bubble Talk: AI-Guided Exhibition Tour
description: This experience invites participants to test Bubble Talk, an experimental AI-guided exhibition tour. Bubble Talk creates personalized tours based on visitors’ interests while introducing unexpected connections to unfamiliar artworks. Participants explore the Connected Earth exhibition in the Ars Electronica Center, share feedback and contribute to research on how AI can help museums foster curiosity, learning and dialogue beyond personal information bubbles.

title: Expert Tour: Christl Baur (DE)
description: Join Christl Baur, Head of the Ars Electronica Festival and Program Director, as she takes you on a guided tour through the theme exhibition Negotiating Humanity. She shares insights into this year’s award-winning works and explores how art can become an infrastructure of negotiation, showing how the topics of the six works on view shape the discussion around this year’s festival theme.

title: Layers of Time: City Tour meets Media Arts (DE)
description: Discover Linz through the lens of Ars Electronica. This tour explores the historic festival venues, revealing their architectural and cultural significance—from monasteries and schools to museums. Wolfram Starczewski, city guide in Linz, together with Ars Electronica Festival Guides, creates a dialogue between the locations of the festival, their (historical) meaning and the artworks presented in the venues.

title: Layers of Time: City Tour meets Media Arts (EN)
description: Discover Linz through the lens of Ars Electronica. This tour explores the historic festival venues, revealing their architectural and cultural significance—from monasteries and schools to museums. Wolfram Starczewski, city guide in Linz, together with Ars Electronica Festival Guides, creates a dialogue between the locations of the festival, their (historical) meaning and the artworks presented in the venues.

title: KEPLER SALON EXTRA EXTERN: SHOW ME YOUR FACE
description: KEPLER SALON EXTRA EXTERN explores the interplay between genetics, experience and identity, questioning deterministic views of human behavior, particularly violence. A two-channel video installation using AI, moving images, text and the sonification of genomic data makes the phenotype tangible as a process of becoming between biological potential and lived experience. The discussion features Johannes Pröll, Mika Kavdanska and Dilmana Yordanova with host Cornelia Lehner.

title: Spotlight Tour FESTIVAL WALK: Negotiating the Real (DE/Austrian Sign Language)
description: How do we negotiate reality? How does community form, both among us humans and with other living beings? What systems of belief shape the conflicts we face in this process and what role does technology play? This guided tour takes you on a journey along the FESTIVAL WALK through the heart of Linz visiting a school, a museum, a hospital and several churches, connecting infrastructures of our daily life with artistic projects.

title: Ars Electronica Solutions Tour (DE)
description: During this tour of the Ars Electronica Solutions showcase, we offer personal insights into our ways of working and the development of the exhibition. We show how innovative concepts emerge from initial ideas, questions and technological possibilities and how they are transformed into immersive experiences through creative processes, interdisciplinary collaboration and the use of cutting-edge technologies. Visitors will discover how content, data and complex interrelationships can become interac

title: Anatomy for Everyone
description: Anatomy for Everyone invites audiences to explore the human body in an immersive virtual anatomy theater. Led by JKU Professor Franz Fellner, giant 3D visualizations generated from CT and MRI data reveal organs, muscles, vessels and bones in remarkable detail. Visitors experience the body layer by layer, discovering how immersive visualization and cinematic rendering are transforming medicine, medical education and scientific communication while making complex anatomy accessible to everyone.

title: How to create a monotype
description: The monotype printmaking technique is demonstrated in this workshop. Believed to have been invented by Giovanni Benedetto Castiglione in the 17th century, it has since become a popular medium for artists seeking to create unique and highly expressive works. Monotype encourages spontaneity and experimentation, fostering creativity, flexibility and an openness to unexpected results.

title: Town Hall Meeting: Art & Culture as Innovation Drivers in AI Infrastructures
description:
As Europe builds out its network of AI factories and High Performance Computing (HPC) centers, a critical question remains largely unaddressed: What role can artists and cultural organizations play in shaping these infrastructures—not as end-users, but as genuine innovation partners?
This Town Hall brings together artists, HPC operators and cultural institutions for an open exchange on how artistic practice can become a recognized driver of innovation within AI networks. Artists working at the f

title: Soil Rendezvous
description: Connect across disciplines, exchange ideas, get inspired by artistic methodologies and help cultivate a growing community around soil literacy and ecological transition. You are invited to take this opportunity to expand your network and contribute to a growing community of change-makers, exploring soil as both climate infrastructure and cultural commons. Plant the seeds for future collaboration!

title: ECOfem Media Art Stammtisch
description: How can female media artists explore nature, ecofeminism, body politics and inclusive futures? How might gender equality and power shape the future of artistic and scientific practices? How can personal experiences from digital artists who work with scientists contribute to environmental stewardship and climate justice? This event will encourage an in-depth public conversation about ecology, outdated political paradigms and contribute to a deeper conversation about the kind of future we wish to

title: Seeds of the Unthinkable
description: Seeds of the Unthinkable is a world-building game which protests the failure of imagination that keeps broken food systems going. Developed by the Institute for Wicked Problems (INVI) and the University of Copenhagen, the game moves through three acts covering what lives in our soils, how soil health connects to human health and what we will eat in 2050. Visitors encounter AI-generated images rooted in both research and science fiction, and will guess which prompts created them, write postcards

title: Performances at Main Square
description: The Flood the Zone with Courage program presents a series of interventions, each lasting no more than seven minutes. Through diverse artistic approaches, these interventions reimagine protest, exploring the many forms it can take and inviting audiences into concentrated moments of action that continuously shift in both form and intensity. This year’s program explores many of the challenges that shape our everyday lives. Some interventions respond to the climate crisis and explore how technologic

title: NaturArchy: Curating Across Art, Science, Policymaking
description: This Town Hall event presents NaturArchy as a case study for working across art, science and policymaking. Drawing on the recent publication and the 14 art-science-policy projects it documents, this event provides a space for participants to share their own projects and reflect on how these practices affect decision-making processes. Discussions will reflect on curatorial practices, science-for-policy, governance and transdisciplinarity.

title: Deer Hunter
description:
Join Andrew Herzog for a screening of his award-winning film Deer Hunter. The event consists of a 30-minute screening followed by a 15-minute conversation. In Deer Hunter, Herzog intertwines archival footage, family home videos and AI-generated imagery to reflect on masculinity, migration, family and identity.

title: Spray and Pray
description:
Join Veneta Androva for a screening of her new film Spray and Pray, recipient of an Honorary Mention in the Prix Ars Electronica 2026. The screening is followed by a conversation with the artist.  
 
Spray and Pray is a speculative animated documentary examining monetized disinformation infrastructures known as mushroom websites—networks of automatically generated news sites designed to launder propaganda and generate advertising revenue. title: AI’s Silent Omissions
description:
Join Nozomu Kubota for a screening of his documentary AI’s Silent Omissions, recipient of an Honorary Mention in the Prix Ars Electronica 2026, Digital Humanity category. The event consists of a 30-minute screening followed by a 15-minute conversation.

title: Data Workers’ Inquiry
description:
Join Milagros Miceli for a presentation of Data Workers’ Inquiry, recipient of the Award of Distinction in the Prix Ars Electronica 2026, Digital Humanity category. The event consists of a 30-minute presentation, followed by a 15-minute conversation.

description:
Join Ryat Yezbick for a live performance of The Innocence of Unknowing, recipient of an Honorary Mention in the Prix Ars Electronica 2026, New Animation Art category.

The project investigates how mass shootings are mediated, staged and normalized through broadcast news. title: Border Tuner | Sintonizador Fronterizo
description:
Join Rafael Lozano-Hemmer for a lecture on Border Tuner, followed by a screening of the documentary and a presentation of the accompanying publication. Together, they offer an in-depth look at the conception and legacy of this large-scale participatory artwork.
