title: The Game Was Rigged from the Start
description:
Join 2girls1comp for a Meet the Artist session exploring how video game modding can be used as a subversive artistic practice. Together, the three works reveal how modding can become a form of critical intervention: by altering rules, animations and glitches within a commercial game, 2girls1comp exposes the ideologies embedded in its systems and opens up possibilities for imagining them differently.
 
Dancing Plague is an adaptation of the world-famous open-world computer game Grand Theft Auto V

title: Best Student Animations from HSLU
description: This screening presents a selection of 13 student films from the Animation program at Lucerne School of Design, Film and Art (HSLU), one of the world’s leading institutions for animation education. Traditionally committed to the artistic auteur film, the Animation study program fosters a holistic understanding of the medium and offers students a highly individualized education across all areas of the discipline, encompassing both artistic auteur filmmaking and applied animation projects.

title: Die Böden der Linzer Donau – einst, heute & in Zukunft
description: The Soil Walk leads into the industrial heart of Linz, to the Klimaoase (Climate Oasis) of the Verein Schwemmland. At the more than 550-year-old Hollaberer estate—the last farming and fishing homestead in Linz—you’ll learn about the cultural and natural history of Lustenau. The focus is on conveying what the Linz alluvial soils have done (and can still do) for climate, nature and environmental protection on a local level. The tour also offers a visionary look at the potential of the Danube soils

title: Robertina Šebjanič – Journal from the TARA expedition vessel: Echoes of the Abyss
description: Echoes of the Abyss addresses the overlooked issue of chemical weapons dumped on the ocean floor. These remnants of past conflicts threaten biodiversity, alter water chemistry and act as environmental time bombs. Based on research conducted during the artist’s expedition with the Tara Ocean Foundation in the Baltic Sea, the talk hosted by researchers from the Catholic Private University Linz explores the intersection of artistic research, marine science, history and ecological destruction.

title: fem(with)me
description: This workshop explores how femininity can be consciously embodied and made visible as a language of presence, confidence and self-expression. It is led by Black Pearl, protagonist of the Extended Reality work OYA, which traces her journey of becoming—a reflection on release, liberation and returning to the self. After a warm-up and a short introduction to Ballroom culture and its roots in New York, participants practice European Runway: poses, walking, turns and a short battle.

title: Character Lab: Digital Companions for a Festival of the Future
description: The workshop explores what kind of personality a digital guide should have at a festival like Ars Electronica. Sincere, playful, poetic or critical? Participants create original AI companion characters, then translate them into simple chatbot prototypes and test first conversations. The event connects character creation, storytelling and AI prompting, raising questions about voice, social cues, trust and mediation in future cultural and artistic AI applications.

title: Endless Possibilities
description:
Deep Space is an open platform, and its possibilities grow through the people who create for it. This session brings together members of the global Deep Space Community to present what they are currently developing—from interactive applications and stereoscopic 3D experiences to video productions and entirely new formats.

title: Science Experience
description: Protect Our Planet and Climate—a Science Experience by Ars Electronica Solutions and the European Space Agency. Over the course of 30 minutes, we will cover a variety of topics from our home planet to planetary defence: Earth observation and climate data reveal our planet’s current state, ESA satellites deliver the facts and the Hera mission provides the platform for an important conversation about how we defend ourselves against asteroids. title: Updating the Great Acceleration Charts: New Signals for a Changing World
description: The Great Acceleration charts made planetary change perceptible and in doing so, changed how humans and nonhumans perceive, feel and act. This workshop treats those affects as data. After a brief introduction to the charts, participants work in small groups to trace how the curves ripple through their own lives and organisations and to translate these ripples into candidate signals for an expanded chart set. title: Future Screenshots
description: Future Screenshots asks: What if we could reach into a possible future, unlock a phone and take a screenshot? In this workshop, audiences draft messages, maps, prompts and posts from worlds that do not yet exist. By mapping, comparing and presenting these everyday digital traces, the workshop explores how our anticipation of change and stability shapes our technological and political imagination—and how the futures people imagine together can become the futures they begin to create.

description:

description:
Deep Space can be more than an immersive venue. Within a city, it can become shared infrastructure for culture, science, education, tourism and public exchange.

description: Curator and Head of Prix Ars Electronica, Emiko Ogawa, will guide us through the exhibition Negotiating Humanity in Lentos Kunstmuseum Linz. This exhibition showcases the award-winning projects of this year’s Prix Ars Electronica and STARTS Prize. These six works set the overall thematic tone for the festival and its many exhibitions. Join the guided tour to engage in a dialogue with the people who help shape the festival.

title: Artist Walk Tour: Negotiating Beyond Humanity
description: Much of life unfolds through forms of perception and communication that remain beyond immediate human experience. Bringing together artistic and scientific perspectives, this artist-guided tour explores smell, vibration, colour and microbial exchange as ways of sensing and relating across species. It invites participants to consider how expanding perception can open new understandings of coexistence and ecological interdependence.

title: Expert Tour FESTIVAL WALK: Christl Baur (DE)
description: The exhibition Negotiating the Real – The Desire to Believe asks which systems of belief and worldviews underpin our social order—and, in turn, shape our understanding of what it means to be human. Christl Baur, Head of the Ars Electronica Festival and Program Director, takes you on a tour along the FESTIVAL WALK. Together, you explore the thematical threads of the exhibition across its different venues in the heart of Linz.

title: Futurelab Networking: Art Science Research
description: For anyone navigating the evolving landscape of Art Science Research, join us in the Futurelab Lounge at Open Futurelab. Let’s step beyond the academic buzzwords to decode the real future of this field: where the funding is moving to, which institutions and industries are reframing themselves to facilitate collaboration, and how education is adapting. Florian Wiencek (LIT Open Innovation Center at JKU Linz) guides visitors through the exhibition Creativity Matters, developed within the Interreg project KreATivita&InovaCZe, showcasing projects from South Bohemia and Upper Austria. title: Open Futurelab Tour (DE)
description:
At the Ars Electronica Futurelab, Ars Electronica’s artistic R&D laboratory and atelier, we believe that the future does not simply arrive: It emerges through dialogue and our actions in the present.
Join our guided tour to experience our latest prototypes at the Open Futurelab and the exhibition Hello Worlds! Here, art and science become methods for exploration, and collaboration a condition through which futures take shape.

title: DAS Trail Workshop for Youngsters
description: DAS Trail is a fieldwork program developed as part of the Data Art & Science Project. In this workshop for kids and teens, you will learn about the local area through data collection. Together with other families, you will walk along specially curated trails in Linz and explore the city from a new perspective through observation, Gaussian Splatting 3D scanning of your discoveries and engaging in dialogue with others.

title: Artist Walk Tour: Negotiating Beyond Humanity
description: Beneath our feet, soil sustains complex relationships that connect microorganisms, fungi, plants and countless other forms of life. This artist-guided tour explores how artistic research can deepen our understanding of these hidden ecologies, revealing soil as a living system rather than a passive resource. From microbial processes to changing landscapes, it invites new ways of sensing, knowing and caring for the ground that supports us.

title: JKU medFOCUS Tour
description: Hosted by the Faculty of Medicine of Johannes Kepler University Linz, this exclusive tour offers behind-the-scenes access to the state-of-the-art medical laboratories at Kepler University Hospital. Visitors explore the cardiac catheterization lab, dermatology with advanced 3D melanoma skin scanning and the 3D printing lab while meeting experts on site. The event showcases the cutting-edge technologies that are driving innovation in research, diagnosis and patient care.

title: Best-of 3D JKU medSPACE
description: At JKU medSPACE, visitors are invited to experience current developments in medicine, teaching and research first-hand. JKU university clinics and institutes present virtual anatomy and demonstrate how 3D operations open up new perspectives on the heart, brain, abdomen, shoulder and eye. The program shows how digital technologies can expand our understanding of the human body, medical education and research. title: JKU Art & Science Tour (DE)
description: The guided tour leads through the JKU MED Campus, where art, science and public discourse meet. Along the way, it features JKU projects, including the exhibition of the Linz Institute of Technology (LIT), projects by the ArtxScience School for Transformation and highlights from the Faculty of Medicine at JKU Linz. The tour explores how curiosity connects research, creativity and society, offering glimpses into possible futures.

title: Ars Electronica Nightline
description: What happens when negotiation is not conducted through words, but through bodies, frequencies and collective presence? At a time when words become weapons and language grows harsher, the Nightline creates a counter-model: a physical, shared space where different perspectives do not inevitably harden into irreconcilable opposites, but can meet and engage with one another. title: Who Heals Tomorrow? AI, Medicine and the Future of Decision-Making
description: Will AI replace doctors in the future? Who is liable when incorrect decisions are made? And what does health data without borders actually mean? In a fishbowl format, experts from the fields of medicine, AI research and law will discuss the opportunities, risks and societal consequences of AI in healthcare together with patient representatives and a live audience. The discussion will outline the enormous possibilities of AI use in medicine, but also address questions of responsibility, patient s

title: Futurelab Night
description: At this year’s Futurelab Night, we celebrate not only the opening of our new exhibition Hello Worlds! but also 30 years of Ars Electronica Futurelab. The long-standing tradition of Futurelab Night as a festival highlight takes on a new form: exploring uncharted territories by transforming multiple floors of the Ars Electronica Center into a shared stage for encounters, exchange and discovery. Through pop-up interventions, performances, demos and conversations, visitors are invited to move throug

title: FARCE
description: FARCE is the project of Vienna-based producer, songwriter, and performer Veronika König. FARCE brings together club music, avant-pop and experimental electronics in a high-energy set that moves between driving dancefloor moments, unexpected turns and unconventional sounds. Combining electronic production, vocals and a love for crossing genres, FARCE creates a space where experimentation and emotion meet. Rooted in Vienna’s independent music scene, FARCE’s work connects pop, club culture and elec

title: Artist Q&A with Joseph Herscher
description: Meet Joseph Herscher, the artist behind Joseph’s Machines—elaborate chain-reaction contraptions that turn everyday objects into unlikely collaborators. In this Q&A session, Herscher talks about the ideas, engineering and endless trial-and-error behind his machines—and what draws him, again and again, to the most complicated way of doing the simplest things.

title: Living Matter
description: Swiss drummer, composer and electronic artist Arthur Hnatek joins transmedia visual artist Sophie Le Meillour for an immersive live A/V performance where acoustic drums become the driving force of a living audiovisual system. Each gesture shapes evolving sound and reactive visuals in real time, transforming rhythm into light, texture and space. Every performance unfolds through improvisation, making each presentation unique.

title: Owelle (live visuals by Structurals)
description: Owelle explores the relationship between identity, corporate culture and transformation through an immersive audiovisual performance. Audiences experience Owelle’s hardware-based live electronics, processed vocals and club-driven rhythms alongside Structurals’ real-time generative visuals and light scenography. Together, sound, light and narrative reshape the stage into a fictional corporate world where performance and space become inseparable.

title: Yao Bobby x Simon Grab
description:
Pan-African rap and noise sound system music.

The Togolese Rapper and political activist Yao Bobby collaborates with Swiss noisemaker Simon Grab. A very raw and unique form of live experimental hip hop—freeform rap and noise.

Each bring a totally singular style and attitude to create a kind of next generation free form rap, noise and synthetic rhythm concoction coaxed out of improvised feedback signals and dynamic microphone control. Yao's lyrics (in his mother tongue Ewé, French and also part

title: ZOBAYDA
description: ZOBAYDA is an Egyptian DJ and multidisciplinary artist based in Amsterdam. Guided by rhythm andpercussion, her sets center energy and the tradition of bringing people together. She blends sounds from the Global South and its diaspora with a disregard for strict genre boundaries. Her practice extends to photography, audio-visual direction, archiving and cultural programming. Exploring storytelling, memory and sound as tools for gathering, reflection and resistance.

title: AI and Property Relations: Who Owns Our Collective Knowledge?
description:
LLMs have been trained on the collective knowledge of humankind. While small copyright violations can land individuals in legal trouble, tech companies are seemingly permitted to train models on hundreds of terabytes of data. Should we demand public ownership of AI models—as Open Source or Open Weights?
This discussion will explore artists’ perspectives and examine how public ownership might help limit the power of tech oligarchs. The session will involve direct input from various artists themse

title: Hadra Rave
description:
Hadra Rave emerges from the artistic encounter between Viennese music producer and artist Seba Kayan and Syrian oud player and composer Orwa Saleh, both established internationally through their solo practices. The project explores how diasporic sound cultures, ritual traditions and contemporary electronic music can create new forms of collective experience.

Combining Seba Kayan’s electronic sound research with Orwa Saleh’s expressive oud playing and improvisation, the project creates a dialogu

title: Join the Rhythm! Samba Percussion Performance and Interactive Drumming Workshop
description: AttacSambaSisters is a women’s and LGBTQ+ inclusive samba drumming group that brings energy, joy and visibility to public demonstrations and community events. Through Brazilian samba rhythms, the performance highlights feminist, queer, climate and social justice causes, using music as a form of peaceful protest and collective expression. This dynamic drumming performance and interactive workshop invites audiences to participate, transforming public space into a vibrant arena of solidarity and en

title: Holy Echo: Clair de Lune
description:
Holy Echo is new sound installation created for St. Mary’s Cathedral. It proposes that a space becomes sacred when human perception is reorganized through an extraordinary acoustic field.

In this performance, evala uses the Holy Echo spatial sound system to dissolve the cathedral’s architecture, transforming it into a fluid, otherworldly realm that transcends time and place. Features coloratura soprano Ayako Tanaka as special guest. Her voice is processed by evala in real-time, immersing the au

title: Mapping the Profits with War
description: This workshop outlines who it is that profits from war and geopolitical crises. Through an interactive, participatory format, the audience draws connections between banks, the arms industry, AI and fossil corporations, authoritarian regimes and the far-right, turning the (public) space into a shared mapping exercise. Participants will be able to create protest banners by visualizing those connections and numbers.

title: Militarisation Myth-Buster Training
description: Peace and anti-militarization advocates are often dismissed as being naive or even accused of providing tacit support for authoritarian regimes. This workshop equips participants with solid arguments and talking points to counter such accusations. After a short introduction to various common attack lines, participants practice debate and dialogue skills in either pairs or small groups. The group is then presented with the option to test these arguments out in real conversations in a public space

title: The Art of Protest: Painting Banners That Matter
description: Ever wondered how a few bold words on fabric can shift public opinion? Join Attac activists for a hands-on workshop exploring the power of protest slogans! We shall kick off with a short intro on the politics of banners and share examples of messages that made real impact. Then, grab your paint and team up to design banners with a feminist focus—or craft your own message. All voices welcome, as long as they stand against discrimination.

title: KRRRA
description: NENDA is an actress and musician from the Austrian Tyrolean Alps. As an actor, she is known from series such as The Rising (Sky) and Belgravia: The Next Chapter (MGM+, Amazon). As a musician, NENDA has won several awards for her self-produced music videos, and her debut single Mixed Feelings topped the FM4 annual charts in 2021. In her debut album KRRRA (Autumn 2025), she continues to explore topics such as identity and other socio-political issues.

title: The Elon Musk Antagonist
description: This participatory performance flips the script: instead of destroying the welfare state like Elon Musk & Co., audience volunteers smash the privileges of tech oligarchs and the super-rich. Cardboard boxes labeled “corporate lobbying”, “privatized healthcare”, “rearmament funding” and more sit on a table, awaiting a symbolic wooden “chainsaw”. Volunteers step up, choose a target and demolish it—followed by an interview on their intention, sparking a debate about the politics behind the gesture.

title: Worship
description: The performance presents an exclusive excerpt from Worship, a new contemporary dance work by Drew Jacoby with the 16 dancers of TANZ LINZ. Exploring ritual, devotion and collective experience beyond religion, it draws on archetypal figures and the idea of the “Divine Feminine”. In the unique setting of St. Mary’s Cathedral, movement, sound and architecture merge into an immersive experience, offering a first glimpse of the upcoming world premiere Divine Matter, a double bill by TANZ LINZ, premie

title: Glitch & Leak: Overflowing Bodies in Public Space at Domgasse
description:
Glitch & Leak is an invitation to open up a space together: a space of disruption, permeability, collective imagination and transformation. The glitch is not an error in the system, but a strategy of resistance—a way of interrupting established patterns and creating openings for other possibilities.
These patterns are also embedded in public space. Public space is never neutral. It is shaped by social, political and economic power relations, which determine who can access it, how it can be used

title: Glitch & Leak: Overflowing Bodies in Public Space at Main Square
description:

title: Polaris
description: Polaris, the latest Pianographique production by Maki Namekawa and Cori O'Lan, offers a distinctive take on the music of Philip Glass, whose compositions have become, for many, a timeless soundtrack of our present moment. Drawing on piano arrangements by Philip Glass himself as well as by Michael Riesman, Maki Namekawa has curated a unique program for this evening, one that speaks directly to the festival’s theme.

title: Destituent Laughing Choir
description: This project uses collective, public laughter as a tactical, non-verbal strategy to confront and disrupt existing power structures, acting as a raw detonator against societal apathy and filling the public space with a disorienting cacophony of irony, joy and profound systemic discomfort. It is structured as a horizontal and open performance around a core group of trained members, inviting the everyday public to organically merge into a massive, contagious feedback loop that renders the mechanics

title: Negotiating Democracy at the OpenDemocracyLab
description: Our democracies and constitutions rest on foundations that were originally laid in a very different world. As societies confront multiple, interconnected crises, many are asking whether our political systems are still equipped to meet today’s challenges. In this participatory workshop, IG Demokratie invites participants to explore the roots of the current crisis of democracy. What lies at its core? Political parties? Patriarchal structures? Escalating techno-capitalism? Or something else entirel

title: Addressing Tomorrow
description:
As part of the Ars Electronica Festival, Calle Libre Street Art Festival and Austrian Post invite visitors to participate in the Addressing Tomorrow Postcard Illustration Workshop.
For generations, postcards have connected people by carrying memories, messages and ideas across places and time. Inspired by the theme Addressing Tomorrow, this workshop transforms the traditional postcard into a creative medium for imagining and communicating personal visions of a better future.
Guided by the Calle

title: Post Compost – Forest Reset
description: The ecological consequences of large-scale monocultures are becoming increasingly evident in European forests. The project centers on a large freestanding billboard installed in public space. Over the course of the festival, large-format posters are added successively to its surface, gradually transforming the image and revealing the project’s research process as a public, time-based intervention.

title: Networking: Art Thinking
description: How can we apply art for innovation and a better future society? Ars Electronica’s Art Thinking is a creative mindset shaping our approach to these futures—and what’s more, it is a highly customizable step-by-step process to transform visions into tangible prototypes that invite public dialog about these futures. The Art Thinking method serves as a starting point for numerous projects, bridging artistic work from the vast Ars Electronica network with creative questions that are essential, challe

title: mozXR: Empowering Creative Minds in XR
description: MozXR is an open-source framework for creating interactive and immersive XR experiences in 2D and 3D. Developed by Mozarteum University Salzburg and Ars Electronica Futurelab, its purpose is to reduce technical complexity so artists can focus on their concepts and creative ideas. Join the developers, artists and researchers behind the project as they share insights into MozXR’s development, its potential for creative practice and new possibilities for creating immersive experiences.

title: Spotlight Tour FESTIVAL WALK: Negotiating the Real (EN)
description: How do we negotiate reality? How does community form, both among us humans and with other living beings? What systems of belief shape the conflicts we face in this process and what role does technology play? This guided tour takes you on a journey along the FESTIVAL WALK through the heart of Linz visiting a school, a museum, a hospital and several churches, connecting infrastructures of our daily life with artistic projects.

title: Spotlight Tour FESTIVAL WALK: Negotiating the Real (DE)

What systems of belief shape the conflicts we face in this process and what role does technology play? This guided tour takes you on a journey along the FESTIVAL WALK through the heart of Linz visiting a school, a museum, a hospital and several churches, connecting infrastructures of our daily life with artistic projects.

title: Spotlight Tour: Negotiating Humanity (EN)
description:
What can we negotiate when it comes to humanity? What must remain non-negotiable? How do we engage with conflicts on an individual and collective level? And what role does art play in this process?

In our daily guided tours, we will be looking for answers to those questions in dialogue with you. This guided tour takes you through the exhibition Negotiating Humanity at Lentos Kunstmuseum, presenting six award-winning projects from the Prix Ars Electronica and STARTS Prize.

title: Spotlight Tour: Negotiating Humanity (DE)
description:

In our daily guided tours, we will be looking for answers to those questions in dialogue with you. This guided tour takes you through the exhibition Negotiating Humanity at Lentos Kunstmuseum, presenting six award-winning projects from the Prix Ars Electronica and STARTS Prize.

description:
You don’t know where to start? Come join one of our Intro Sessions. Our art educators offer you in-depth insights into selected projects from the festival’s most important exhibitions. Whether you’re curious, critical or at the very beginning of your festival visit, these sessions are the perfect introduction to learning about how art, technology and society intersect.

description:
It all starts at 3:00 PM at the Lentos Kunstmuseum with a premiere. Hemma Schmutz (Director of the Lentos Kunstmuseum) and Gerfried Stocker (Artistic Director) invite guests to the opening of NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – Award-Winning Works Exhibition, which for the first time brings together the projects of the winners of the Prix Ars Electronica and the European Union’s S+T+ARTS Prize and takes on the festival theme.

At 5:00 PM sharp, Brigitte Hütter (Rector of the University of Arts Linz) and Manu

title: Town Hall Meeting: Conflict Culture
description: At the heart of this year’s festival lies the conviction that art can function as an infrastructure for negotiation, not as a place of judgement, but rather as a space for productive discomfort, ambivalence and confrontation. A place in which dissent is not concealed but acknowledged, and in which conflicts are not resolved but made workable. This informal gathering is an invitation to think through what this means in practice. How do societies maintain the capacity for genuine disagreement with

title: Studio Sessions
description: Studio Sessions offer a space for experimental and playful performances at Studio 1 of the University of Arts Linz. The spectrum ranges from complex audiovisual pieces and text and dance performances to instrumental spatial and sound art experiences. Alongside well-established performance formats, unconventional experiments are also part of this series, which has become a popular event within the Ars Electronica Festival and complements the campus exhibition of the Time-Based and Interactive Med

title: New Perspectives on Salzburg
description: The new exhibition venue Orangery Salzburg – Panorama | World Heritage re-contextualizes cultural heritage not as a static archive, but as a space for interactive, shared experience. How can digital technologies open new ways of seeing, understanding, negotiating and collectively experiencing cultural heritage? Salzburg Museum and Ars Electronica Futurelab discuss this through showcasing one of the new interventions. At its core is Johann Michael Sattler’s panoramic view of Salzburg (1825–1829),

title: Ars Electronica Opening
description: Under the title NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – FUTURE BEGINS, the festival puts fundamental questions about humanity up for negotiation. On the opening night, a clear declaration is made: a commitment to humanity—more precisely, to the unbreakable humanity found in art and in the shared experience of it. St. Mary’s Cathedral, with its overwhelming spatial and acoustic scale, becomes the resonating chamber for this declaration. Here, the most diverse musical languages and worldviews of the past five cent

title: Big Concert Night 2026
description:
Polaris – Music Between the Poles

This year, Ars Electronica’s Big Concert Night unfolds as a multimedia Gesamtkunstwerk. Staged across three concert halls, visitors move between strikingly different concerts and performances, each performed several times throughout the evening so that audiences can experience them in shifting constellations and atmospheres.
Polaris—the pole star and fixed point of this constellation—embodies the festival’s guiding theme: the question of what it fundamentally m

title: From Collection to Connection
description: How can collections evolve from repositories of history into catalysts for dialogue, participation and innovation? Bringing together leaders from museums, foundations, artistic practice and creative technology, From Collection to Connection explores how to transform archives into multimedial experiences. We look  at cultural heritage in motion, where objects, stories and memories begin to move beyond preservation and become invitations to connect, reinterpret and imagine futures together.

title: Beyond Reconstruction: Digital Heritage and Cultural Resilience
description: Cultural heritage sites are fragile, from threats like devastating fires to utter destruction by armed conflicts. What role can technology and art play in conservation efforts for world heritage? In this panel discussion between the creators behind Unbreakable Ukraine and Ars Electronica, we even want to go one step further: What role can technology and art play in moving from conservation or reconstruction to cultural resilience? Memory becomes a conscious act of resistance, underlining the imp

title: Curator’s Tour with Julia Staudach: “Collection Francisco Carolinum”
description: With the Collection Francisco Carolinum, the museum presents its continuously growing collection of blockchain-based art in a comprehensive exhibition for the first time. Since its launch in 2021, the collection has grown to include works on the Ethereum, Tezos and Bitcoin blockchains, offering a window into an artistic field that remains in constant flux. In this tour, the exhibition’s curator, Julia Staudach, shares insights into the artworks and the ideas behind them.

title: Artist Tour with Ana María Caballero and Curator Julia Staudach: “READ THE ROOM”
description: In this Artist Tour, artist and poet Ana María Caballero joins curator Julia Staudach to guide visitors through Read the Room, her first institutional mid-career retrospective. The exhibition spans key works in installation, performance, sculpture, choreography, cinematic AI and literature. Together, they offer insight into an artistic practice rooted in a fundamental conviction: language is not a fixed medium, but a living process that unfolds in the interplay of writing and reading.

title: Artist Tour with Claudia Larcher and Curator Eva Fischer: “No applause. no life. no pain.“
description: In this guided tour, Claudia Larcher joins the curator of the exhibition, Eva Fischer, to explore how her works in the exhibition No applause. no life. no pain. at Francisco Carolinum unfold a panorama of change: the extinction of species, the erosion of shared cultural spaces and the transformation of our perception in the age of generative AI. In her films, installations and AI-based works, Claudia Larcher connects ecological questions with reflections on the future of cinema and image product

title: Reading the Room: Language, Systems, and Contemporary Art
description: Reading the Room: Language, Systems, and Contemporary Art brings together Manuela Naveau, Ana María Caballero, Sergio Fontanella and Alfred Weidinger on a panel moderated by Julia Staudach. A conversation rooted in Caballero’s first institutional retrospective. Taking the exhibition (and the page) as its point of departure, this panel explores poetry as a contemporary artistic medium, examining language, translation, participation and systems of record-keeping within contemporary new media setti

title: Patterns & Politics: Book Presentation and Panel
description: This book presentation and panel brings together Claudia Hart, Andrew Blanton and Anika Meier for a conversation, moderated by curator Julia Staudach, on Hart’s artistic practice and her first museum retrospective. Taking the exhibition Patterns and Politics and the publication as its point of departure, the panel traces Hart’s perspective on technology, visual culture and power, connecting her decades of work with virtual image-making to current debates on AI art.

title: GRMW Haunted Nightline
description:
On Friday, September 11th, and Saturday, September 12th, Stadtwerkstatt will host two nights of: GET READY for haunted nightline!

The GRWM4 HAUNTED NIGHTLINE features hybrid genres, abstract practices, electronic soundscapes, and a ghost train ride with living, dead, and undead media. The program was co-curated by Gabriela Gordillo and STWST.

Musicians, sound artists, and performers from Linz and around the world will haunt the night with vibration-inducing acts, dystopian ambient sounds, ener

title: Haunted Herstory: Herzblutwiese Stadtwerkstatt – Screening at Milieukino
description: Media art, subculture and fragments and continuities of a tech-oriented feminist history. The essay film Herzblutwiese Stadtwerkstatt addresses feminism, equal rights and gender equality at the Stadtwerkstatt, the longest-running autonomous art and culture space in the city of Linz. The essay film Herzblutwiese Stadtwerkstatt addresses feminism, equal rights and gender equality at the Stadtwerkstatt, the longest-running autonomous art and culture space in the city of Linz. title: Die fliegende Holländerin kehrt zurück
description: With projectors, text, broadcasts, wild gestures and media of all kind, the milieu cinema is being taken over.

title: Haunted by Repetition
description: Participatory Reading and Discussion: Bianca Ludewig will read from her book Transmedia Festivals – Audio-Social Communities Between Artistic Experimentation and Economization alongside guests. This will be followed by a discussion with sound artists Anna S. Adelt, Stefan Tiefengraber, and Sashe Urdovski, who are presenting works at STWST.

title: HandsOn: Man x Machine
description: How close can robots actually get to us? From prosthetics that replace lost abilities, and exoskeletons that support and strengthen us, to robots that accompany and assist us—this HandsOn presentation demonstrates robotics as a technology of closeness. Together with the audience, this session will explore the relationship between humans and machines.

title: Sinécdoque: The Prosthetic Self
description: Berenice Olmedo’s work challenges the idea of the human body as autonomous and complete. Drawing on disability studies and cyborg theory, her sculptures explore the body as inherently relational, shaped by technologies, care, and interdependence. In dialogue with philosophy, this talk, which is hosted by researchers of the Catholic Private University Linz, examines notions of incompleteness, connection and transformation, asking how prosthetic technologies reshape our understanding of embodiment

title: Creative Coding Open House (SAT 12.9.)
description: Whether you are a novvvvice or enjoying vvvv professionally, join us for an afternoon of demos. Bring your own patch or just check out what is on display. We will be avateering virtual characters, have a laser to play with and maybe even a robot. But most importantly we will be curious to hear your thoughts and questions about vvvv and to share what we know.

title: Creative Coding Open House (THU 10.9.)
description: Let’s get a taste of different creative coding tools and discuss the philosophies behind them. Find out what they have in common and what is unique about them. Bring your own favorite tool and share your experience with it as we build the same artwork in parallel. We will have stations where beginners can taste-test different tools and find what is right for you!

title: Creative Coding Open House (WED 9.9.)
description: The Creative Coding Open House starts with a day to meet fellow creative coding tool users and makers (and those who are just curious!). Make new connections and catch up with old friends. Pitch activities for the coming days at the Open House and help us make this a cozy space to hang out.

title: Creative Coding Open House (FRI 11.9.)
description: At the Creative Coding Open House, this lab demystifies how to support open-source software. Designed for all skill levels, the event guides participants through taking their contributing first steps, making great tutorials and improving documentation and language support. Attendees gain practical experience committing code while exploring meaningful ways of supporting communities. This hands-on day empowers everyone to sustain the creative digital tools that they love.

title: Creative Coding Open House (SUN 13.9.)
description: Have you ever wanted to try out Processing or p5.js? Join us for a day celebrating 25 years of Processing—a gathering for beginners, experienced users and everyone in between. Come by to see how easily hands, faces and bodies can be tracked with ml5.js and p5.js, explore how Processing can be used to create immersive Deep Space applications, discuss what is next for Processing and p5.js or exchange ideas about using AI tools in your creative practice or teaching.

title: DIE KUNSTSCHAFFENDEN | Meet the Artist: Robert Moser
description:
Meet artist Robert Moser for a conversation on the exhibition In the Paradise of Painting. Or: On Growth and Refinement, on view at DIE KUNSTSCHAFFENDEN. As high-performance computers increasingly assess human beings by their “market value”, art remains a space for growth and refinement. At its most authentic, it preserves what makes us human. In this light, hand-painted works become an act of resistance. 
The artist will share insights into his practice and reflect on painting as a space for hu

title: PULS
description: PULS explores the boundaries and peculiarities of our perception through the use of sensory extremes. Flashing light, total darkness and brief audiovisual impulses repeating at rates between rhythm and tone will manipulate our sense of time and space. The installation will overwhelm us, create illusions, force us to change perspectives or even bring us to different state of consciousness.

title: Grassroots Innovators
description: How do grassroots communities become engines of innovation? This Town Hall, hosted by Schmiede Hallein, opens up questions from Rewilding Cultures: collaborative production, inclusive participation and sustainable practice. For 20+ years Schmiede has built a “do it with others” culture—trust and curiosity as productive forces. Short intro, then open exchange. No finished answers—just the practices that let responsible innovation happen.

title: Negotiating Reality – Conflict Culture,  AI and Democracy in the Digital Public Sphere
description:
Democracy has always depended on places where different perspectives can meet, disagreement can be negotiated and shared futures can be imagined. Today, many of these encounters take place online, in digital spaces shaped by the logics of attention, amplification and emotional engagement. Here, disagreement can easily turn into polarization and fragmentation, while disinformation is increasingly used to deepen social divides, undermine trust and advance geopolitical interests.

title: Creativity as civic infrastructure: CCIs and digital commons
description: The event is part of ekip, a Horizon Europe project, funded by the EU. It explores how cultural and creative industries can strengthen Europe’s digital commons as civic infrastructure. Through discussion and exchange, participants will formulate EU-level policy recommendations to support CCIs and their open innovation capacity.

title: JKU Art & Science Tour (EN)
description: The guided tour leads through the JKU MED Campus, where art, science and public discourse meet. Along the way, it features JKU projects, including the exhibition of the Linz Institute of Technology (LIT), projects by the ArtxScience School for Transformation and highlights from the Faculty of Medicine at JKU Linz. The tour explores how curiosity connects research, creativity and society, offering glimpses into possible futures.

title: Expert Tour FESTIVAL WALK: Christl Baur (EN)
description: The exhibition Negotiating the Real – The Desire to Believe asks which systems of belief and worldviews underpin our social order—and, in turn, shape our understanding of what it means to be human. Christl Baur, Head of the Ars Electronica Festival and Program Director, takes you on a tour along the FESTIVAL WALK. Together, you explore the thematical threads of the exhibition across its different venues in the heart of Linz.

title: DorfTV – Radical Broadcast
description:
DorfTV – Radical Broadcast transforms the Kunstuni Campus into an experimental television zone somewhere between loss of control, improvisation and grandeur. Under this motto, a show emerges that dares to evolve while it is happening: wild live broadcasts, risky decisions, technical experiments and interactions with visitors and artists who are either courageous—or simply careless.
A specially appointed jury evaluates everything in real time: Who is acting bravely? Who is completely overestimati

title: drag your world. Youth Exchange Project Presentation
description:
On the last day of the festival, the final presentation of the Youth Exchange Project will take place.

For the Youth Exchange Project, young people from different countries come together in Linz for a cultural and artistic exchange in the context of the Ars Electronica Festival. A multifaceted project takes shape during the festival that brings together creatives and socially engaged individuals between 16 and 20 years old.

title: Press Start – RADICAL GAMING Performance
description: Press Start is a performance that involves dance, music and spoken word. It explores the challenges faced by a young individual who is pulled into a radical online universe through gaming, where they encounter manipulation, controlling behavior and bullying.

title: Genome Sonification

Through moving image, text, AI-mediated visual transformation and direct sonification of genomic data, the project explores phenotype as a process of becoming. title: Live Cinema Lab
description: The Live Cinema Lab is a participatory film installation that invites participants to actively immerse themselves in the world of filmmaking. The focus is not on the final result, but on the creative process itself: How does a scene emerge? How do decisions, encounters and perspectives shape a story? Participants step into a role and develop a short film scene together with a professional acting partner on site. They experience a glimpse of everyday life on a film set, from preparation and actin

title: Pain: Interconnected with Nature
description: In this workshop, we attune to the earth’s body alongside our own, exploring how environmental loss, ecological grief and planetary suffering are felt in our nervous systems and in our bodies, and how they affect our sense of belonging. Drawing on the concept of inter-being, we expand the notion of pain beyond the individual. When forests burn, species vanish and the world heats up. Where does that solastalgia land in you? title: RISE
description:
This is the premiere of the artist’s new song RISE—a composition that explores ideas of resilience and the process of becoming. It is a journey of rediscovery and reinvention.
Crystn Hunt Akron gained international attention following a live performance in Cairo, where an early audience interruption sparked a widespread debate on issues of artistic freedom, cultural contexts and the role of experimental sound art within religious spaces. title: DAS Trail Workshop
description: DAS Trail is a fieldwork program developed as part of the Data Art & Science Project of Toyota Coniq and Ars Electronica Futurelab. In this workshop, you will learn about the local area through data collection. Together with other participants, you will walk along specially curated trails in Linz and explore the city from a new perspective through observation, Gaussian Splatting 3D scanning of your discoveries and engaging in dialogue with others.

description:
Sound Campus – Listening Underground explores the movement beneath the surface. It considers the ongoing, divergent processes which are felt but not always seen. To submerge opens up new modes of attention and multi-sensory listening that change our relation with the surroundings.

title: Renewable Hydrogen for resilient and emission-free Mobility Systems
description: Decarbonizing the transportation sector is one of the key challenges on the path to climate neutrality. As a zero-emission energy source, hydrogen can make a significant contribution to reducing greenhouse gas emissions while also strengthening energy security through the use of domestic, renewable energy sources. It enables the storage and delivery of renewable energy regardless of when and where it is generated.

title: Meet the Artist: Exploring the Art-Research Project ”Echoes of the Abyss” – Revealing the Ocean’s Hidden Histories and Geopolitical Scars
description: This Meet the Artist event presents Echoes of the Abyss by artist-researcher Robertina Šebjanič and Tina Dolinšek (Projekt Atol), exploring how the toxic legacies of geopolitical conflicts persist in marine environments through dumped chemical munitions and unexploded ordnance. They will introduce the project’s interdisciplinary collaborations between special diving units, marine scientists and artists, revealing the layered processes behind addressing complex ecological and geopolitical histori

title: Kunstuni Linz International Universities Seminar (KLIUS)
description:
The seminar offers educators, students, artists and researchers a platform to present their work and receive constructive feedback. Held during the Ars Electronica Festival, it provides an ideal space for networking and creative exchange among international guests. You are welcome to submit your work as either a digital presentation (such as slides) or an analog poster.

Participants will be grouped into panels of 3–5, depending on the topics of the presentations.

title: NE #00: New Embeddings of/for Artistic Intelligence
description: What forms of Artistic Intelligence become possible when artists, institutions, scientists and technologists organise around shared needs rather than disciplinary boundaries? How can AI support—not determine—those new collaborations? How do we build alternative infrastructures? This embedding event stages the question as an exchange: participants set down what they need, have built, and refuse with AI, cluster where their answers meet and trade concrete offers and requests into a shared ledger.

title: Fluidity of Images: Surrealist Juxtaposition and Image Mixing in Generative AI
description:
What happens when a machine mixes paintings without text prompts? Fluidity of Images explores the juxtaposition space between images: the territory between two source works where they combine to different extents to reveal a spectrum of new forms, condensations and compositions. It situates this practice within a broader continuum of procedural and collective artistic practices, where agency is distributed across processes, tools and collaborators.

title: DANCING DIALOGUES (with(out) AI) …
description:
How can individual movement signatures be mapped, recognised and predicted? 
How can a dancing dialogue with the HAMLET Generative AI tools: Dance Style Analysis and Generation Enabler and the Music-to-Movement Enabler lead to new ways of inhabiting and discovering our bodies through movement, of relating to each other and to the tangibly physical and intangible, intuitively intelligible latent spaces into which we are immersed? The workshop invites participants to dance dialogues with(out) AI.

title: El Cultivo de la Mente – Art Film
description: El Cultivo de la Mente is a performance film by the artist duo Blüten & Papaya, divided into three acts, with a live performance of the soundtrack by Milan Conic on piano. The film centers on a stranded man who devotes himself to self-imposed tasks in support of nature on a solitary island. It interrogates human logic in relation to natural processes and cycles, as well as humanity’s engagement with its own will. Composer and pianist Milan Conic musically immerses himself in the protagonist’s in

title: TiSHiNA (duo)
description:
TıSHıNA blends soulful pop with modern harmonies, hip-hop grooves and electronic elements—a sound that is at once intimate and captivating.

TıSHıNA was founded by Viviane Töbich and Milan Conić, who have been writing songs together since 2020 and formed their band a year later. Since then, they have played numerous concerts on the local scene and built a solid presence there.

The band members’ varied musical and personal backgrounds merge into a sound that invites pause—a blend of calm, soulfu

title: Tarlan Eshtiagh
description:
Tarlan Eshtiagh is an Iranian-born musician, vocalist, pianist and arranger. She is currently based in Austria. Beyond jazz and contemporary vocal art, she has deep roots in Persian music, having worked as singer, pianist and arranger. Notably, they rearranged traditional Persian compositions for piano and vocals.

Tarlan Eshtiagh and Milan Conic are beginning a musical collaboration in Linz. Inspired by traditional Iranian music, they blend electronic sounds with modern arrangements, creating a

title: Te-En Chen
description:
Te-En Chen is a composer, synthesist and sound artist based in Linz, Austria. His work bridges classical tradition and experimental practice through live electronics, modular synthesis, multichannel composition and free improvisation. Combining real-time sound processing with synthesizer performance, he creates immersive sonic dialogues between acoustic instruments and electronic textures in interdisciplinary collaborations.

Composer and synthesist Te-En Chen and pianist/composer Milan Conić fi

title: Tomá Ivanov
description: Tomá Ivanov, formerly half of the techno live act KOMATON, whose track In Between appeared on Cocoon's Compilation J, went on to explore jazz, live electronics and experimental songwriting as TOMÁ before returning to the club with a reduced, personal sound: dusty low-end warmth, tight percussion and melodic restraint.

title: The Unsettled
description:
The Unsettled is the duo project of Serbian jazz pianist Milan Conic and Ukrainian producer J San, merging their individual stories of resilience with an eclectic blend of electronic music. Drawing on genres such as House, UK Garage, and New School Breaks, their sound is enriched by Milan's contemporary piano playing, while J San's innovative sound design adds a distinctive edge.
Crafting immersive atmospheres and intricate sonic textures, they transport listeners into evolving, cinematic yet da

title: Maja Vidic – Free Association Improvisation
description:
Maja Vidic is a Slovenian dancer, choreographer, performer and musician exploring the connection between movement and voice.

Free Association Improvisation is an interdisciplinary artistic project initiated by Milan Conić, exploring the boundaries between music, movement and spontaneous expression.
Rooted in the principle of free association, the project embraces immediacy, intuition and presence—allowing sound, body and visual elements to emerge organically in the moment, without predetermined

title: Milan Conić & Lotte Sandhacker
description: What happens when music and poetry meet? Milan Conić and Lotte Sandhacker play with the piano, voice and musical poetry—separately, together and merged as one.

title: Prototyping Fictions: Workshop and Screening of Ocean Futurisms
description: Ocean Futurisms is a series of animated short films, inviting audiences to step into alternative, science-based futures for the ocean. Designed to be thought-experiments that inspire discussion about real-world change, the films are based on careful research and speculative fiction. This event includes a screening of the films and a hands-on introduction to the world-building approaches behind the project.

title: Little Explorers: Kids’ Tour
description: Join us on a playful journey through projects at the intersection of art, technology and society. Created for children between the ages of four and ten and their accompanying adults, this special tour along the FESTIVAL WALK invites young participants to explore surprising perspectives on this year’s festival topic.

title: Crafting Futures Lab: Re-membering our Seeds
description: Seeds are living archives. They carry memories of place, seasons and generations of care. This collective embroidery circle invites participants to stitch seeds into fabric while listening to stories about plants, place-making and seed keeping. Together, we reflect on how knowledge is embedded in materials and practices—and how, like seeds, it is preserved, transformed and passed on.

title: Crafting Futures Lab: Pulling. Weaving. Connecting. Threads
description: Gold threads once wrapped saints and sovereigns, while today they carry signals, light and touch. In this workshop we follow a filament’s journey, weaving cables that are both ornament and circuit. Along the way we explore how decoration becomes function, how craft becomes technology, and how pulling a single thread can unravel histories.

title: Crafting Futures Lab: Crafting Mountains from Dusty Tales
description: A reading of field notes and laboratory logs on fantastical, mystical, strange and toxic tales of crafted mountains: From crystal growth and lava imitation to mining landfills and heaps of electronic waste—materials scientific research not only works with extracted materials from the undergrounds but is also entangled in the design of new piles of materials. This session gives insights into the research methods of an experimental, embodied and material-based historiography of design which starts

title: Crafting Futures Lab: Unearthing Taste
description: Some forms of preservation can only be accessed through destruction. Unearthing Taste is a food happening and conversation exploring clay-based food preservation, material knowledge and the value of impermanence. Together we break open earthen vessels to share regional food, stories and reflections on care, place, memory and resourcefulness.

title: Crafting Futures Lab: From Textiles to Textures
description: We understand tools as actors in the making of physical things, but also in shaping and preserving memory across generations. In this workshop, we explore the unexpected connections between pasta-making and textile crafts through the tools used in both practices. By handling familiar tools in unfamiliar ways, we revisit and reconsider their stories through the shaping of dough, bringing them into conversation with our own knowledge, memories and understanding of the everyday.

title: Crafting Futures Aperitif: Liquid Archives
description:
Seeds, plants, stones and gold threads form the basis of syrups that translate moments, shared knowledge and experiences from the festival’s workshops, conversations and practices into flavor. Visitors are invited to an aperitif event where they can compose their own drinks and encounter this collection through taste and togetherness.

All welcome. No registration required.

title: Crafting Futures Lab: Crushing the Rocks
description: The Crushing the Rocks workshop explores the technique of textile printing with mineral pigments obtained from locally found rocks and fragments of old bricks. Together, we crush, sift, mix and print, following the transformation of a solid material into a fine powder: the pigment. Participants are invited to observe material transformation, reflect on the origin and value of materials and approach the act of making with curiosity and care rather than fixed expectations.

title: Panel Discussion: Hydrogen and the road ahead: perspectives from Art, Society and BMW
description: This panel looks beyond hydrogen as an engineering topic and explores the broader conditions for technological acceptance. With perspectives from art, society and BMW, the discussion examines what hydrogen technology can contribute to future mobility, how trust in new technologies is built and how creative approaches can open up new ways of engaging with innovation.

title: Hydrogen at the BMW Group Plant Steyr
description: Integrated development and production at one site: BMW Group Plant Steyr and its development center have over 40 years experience in applying new technologies. We are now contributing to pre-series development of the third-generation fuel cell system and preparing for series production of the hydrogen drivetrain.

title: Opening: Living Archives
description: To kick off the day’s focus on Living Archives, Ars Electronica invites you to a 60-minute opening performance in Deep Space 8K. Following a welcome address, Gerfried Stocker guides the audience through selected highlights of this year’s festival program as well as standout projects from the previous year. Archives are commonly regarded as places of preservation—orderly repositories of a complete past. Living Archives challenges this notion by proposing a different understanding: archives as dyn

title: BMW Hydrogen Strategy (EN)
description: This Master Class takes the audience behind the scenes of hydrogen fuel cell technology. Using the upcoming BMW iX5 Hydrogen as an example, it explains how a hydrogen vehicle works, how the fuel cell system generates electric power on board and how BMW integrates key components, such as the third-generation fuel cell system and hydrogen tank technology, into the vehicle's architecture.

title: BMW Hydrogen Strategy (DE)
description: This Master Class takes the audience behind the scenes of hydrogen fuel cell technology. Using the upcoming BMW iX5 Hydrogen as an example, it explains how a hydrogen vehicle works, how the fuel cell system generates electric power on board and how BMW integrates key components, such as the third-generation fuel cell system and hydrogen tank technology, into the vehicle's architecture.

title: Prix Ars Electronica Award Ceremony
description: The Prix Ars Electronica Award Ceremony at the Design Center Linz will be a further highlight of the festival week. On this evening, the focus will lie on art—and with it on the exceptional artists who were awarded the Golden Nica of the Prix Ars Electronica in 2026. In addition, the winners of the S+T+ARTS Prize, the AI for Social Impact Initiative and State of the ART(ist)  will be asked to come on stage.

title: Nadia Struiwigh
description: Nadia Struiwigh is an accomplished Dutch producer and live artist who operates between Rotterdam and Berlin. Drawing upon the Warp school of electronica, her sound bridges deep, beatless ambient immersions and kinetic, hardware-driven techno. With releases on labels like Dekmantel and CPU, as well as a DJ residency at Tresor, her performances—ranging from intimate listening sessions to open-ended, improvised club sets—express a rich, deeply personal sonic world powered by technical mastery and g

title: Olivier Messiaen “Apparition de l'Église éternelle”
description: With Olivier Messiaen’s Apparition de l'Église éternelle, cathedral organist Gerhard Raab brings a monumental masterpiece of modern organ music to the acoustic space of the St. Mary’s Cathedral. Literally translating to the ”Apparition of the Eternal Church”, the piece builds over a relentlessly pulsating bass ostinato into a massive, architectural wave of sound—an immersive experience that unleashes the full physical power of the cathedral organ.

title: Embodied Futures
description: Embodied Futures asks what happens when Mixed Reality becomes not just a virtual world but a space to test new forms of embodiment, identity and relation. Drawing on the research projects OYA and EVERYBODY DANCE NOW (EDN.ALPHA), the Town Hall brings together voices from art, technology and research—and the audience—for an open exchange. Together they explore how immersive technology can lead deeper into the body, and what new forms of learning, empathy and community might emerge.

title: Extended Reality – An Art Form in Public Space  (on Trinity-Tarot-Garden)
description: The event asks what changes when art enters public space as Extended Reality. Its starting point is Trinity-Tarot-Garden by Ugo Dossi and Stefan Göppel, a walkable virtual sculpture park of 28 oversized symbols experienced through VR headsets. Artists, architects, curators and the audience discuss how immersive technology reshapes public space, how cultural heritage such as the symbolic world of the Tarot is passed on, and what it means when a work of art no longer needs a building.

title: ORBIT – A War Series
description: The title Orbit: A War Series is a reference to the New York artist Nancy Spero: deeply moved by the photographs of the Vietnam War that were circulating in the media, Spero investigated the links between sexuality, violence and power in The War Series (1966–70). The subject of oppressive power structures revealed in her art is horrifyingly relevant today. Orbit: A War Series appeals to the images in our minds: Brigitta Muntendorf’s immersive 3D audio space oratorio is like an electroacoustic se

title: STORMO (R)
description: What enables systemic transformation? STORMO®️ is a workshop on collective intelligence that invites participants to embody the relational enablers essential for ecosystem transformation. Inspired by the behaviour of flocks in nature, it creates a space where listening, collaboration, holding space and shared leadership arise through direct experience. It embodies the processes enabling transformation, as elaborated by the Systemic Narratives research carried out by EIT Culture and Creativity.

title: Jamming with and as Pastagang
description: Learn to jam with and as Pastagang: At the heart of it is the live coding language Strudel. For visuals, Pastagang tends to use the visual synthesizer language Hydra. Start from the beginning, no experience is needed.

title: For Sun Ra on Saturn (Against Elon on Mars)
description: This year, a red-lit area will be visible on the Maindeck in front of the STWST. The red area stands for all manner of dramatic expressions. It lies open like a huge, screaming mouth of blood, evoking both the current horrors of the wars plaguing the globe and the structural brutalities of capitalism: Even the concrete screams, to paraphrase Michel Houellebecq. And everything screams—everything that has been torn from life and fed into the current machinery of exploitation—into this new technoca

title: Future Care
description: Explore the future of care in the age of AI and robotics. This open discussion marks the first step in a new research collaboration between Dai Nippon Printing and the Ars Electronica Futurelab. Together, the discussion explores how technology is reshaping well-being and social connection, with a focus on AI and robotics. Participants are invited to help shape the conversation by sharing their visions for the future.

title: Town Hall Meeting: Hello Worlds!
description: The Future Humanity Project is an experimental research collaboration between Ars Electronica Futurelab and Toyota Motor Corporation’s Advanced R&D and Engineering Company. Through artistic research, experimental R&D and public participation, it explores future scenarios around AI and humanity. Hello Worlds! turns this research into a platform where visitors can experience, question and contribute to the research itself. Meet the team and join the conversation.

title: The Humanity Negotiation Quest
description:
Guide yourself through the FESTIVAL WALK and discover the fascinating history behind the historic and everyday locations around OK QUARTER. Win negotiation points. Negotiate four different negotiation zones, where points can be won for Humanity or for the Other.

Collect hidden treasures. Use your phone to collect the hidden treasures marked by NFC stickers at exhibition locations and catch them all to gain new negotiation powers!

Discover your humanity negotiation profile. Find what drives you

title: SoundPark
description: As part of Unglaublicher Herbst, Brucknerhaus Linz and Ars Electronica bring back the beloved SoundPark format to the festival stage. For years it was a fixture of the Big Concert Night, carried by the powerful audio infrastructure that otherwise powers Linz’s Klangwolke, and it transformed Donaupark into a resonating space for electronic music. Along the route from Lentos to the Brucknerhaus, avant-garde electronic sound experiences were broadcast there at full intensity. This year, that tradit

title: Performance: Airy
description: Airy begins with a question: how can we sense what a machine is trying to do when its code remains hidden? Industrial robotic arms lift and snap a sheet of silk as two dancers move with and against them. A projected forest climbs from ground to open sky. Mist gathers when their timing slips and clears when they find a rhythm again. The dancers of TAO Dance Theater do not explain the machines. Through weight, touch, hesitation and recovery, they test how trust is made and lost between human and m

title: 12.5 square meters—space for a car, or…
description:
The project 12,5 Quadratmeter—Platz für ein Auto, oder … (12.5 square meters—space for a car, or…) started with an empty parking space in the schoolyard and the children’s complaints about the lack of space to move around.
This sparked a thought experiment: What could be possible in these 12.5 square meters? After all, it’s not just cars that need space, but also creative ideas for using public space. The students’ visions ranged from a mini-campsite and cozy reading corners to a soccer field. F

title: Bruckner Orchester Linz
description: The question of what it fundamentally means to be human has occupied the thoughtful and searching minds of our species for as long as we can remember. The rapid rise of Artificial Intelligence and digitalization has given this question new urgency, placing it at the heart of the Ars Electronica Festival 2026 under the title NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – FUTURE BEGINS. At its opening, Markus Poschner and the Bruckner Orchester Linz offer three compelling musical responses—the power of which unfold all t

title: Declaring Humanity
description: The multilingual appraoch of the project not only highlights the universal validity of human rights but also reflects the diversity of the citizens of Linz, who are actively involved. In front of St. Mary’s Cathedral, groups of young people from Linz with migrant backgrounds are scattered across the square. They chant parts of the Declaration of Human Rights in their mother tongues. They, along with the audience, become the fierce voice advocating for human rights.

title: 36th VVVV Worldwide Meetup
description:
The 36th VVVV Worldwide Meetup hosted by the VVVV Community at the Ars Electronica Center in Linz is all about the visual programming environment vvvv gamma and its visual language VL. The meetup is open to everyone via Zoom. Join us IRL or online for artist presentations and announcements in the VVVV Community.
Moderated by Randall Vasquez, Simon Weckert and Amir Bastan.

Supported by Studio Brüll & 3e8.studio.
Feel free to connect with us for the next meetup to show your work and join the conv

title: Latin American Networking Gathering
description:
We warmly invite you to a special Latin America networking event—an opportunity for artists, cultural professionals and anyone interested in connecting with the vibrant South American creative community at the Ars Electronica Festival.
This informal gathering is co-hosted by Hauptplatz 23 and the Ars Electronica Festival.
We are especially looking forward to welcoming artists and professionals from Chile, Latin America and beyond. We look forward to sharing it with you.

title: Negotiating Knowledge: Trust in Science in the Digital Age
description: What does it mean to trust science when knowledge is shaped by distributed agencies—researchers, citizens and AI, amplified through digital and social media? Embedded in Climate Agents, this discussion links trust to transparency and participation. We ask how scientific identities, responsibilities and narratives are negotiated, and how shared confidence in these processes can help us shape the future together. Together, we examine scientific progress as an evolving, formalised process.

title: Welcome to Contested Futures
description: Francesca Bria and José Luis de Vicente open the program by naming what is actually being negotiated: not only future technology, but the terms of collective life. Who has the power to shape the future. Whose labour it runs on. What it costs the planet that has to carry it. Europe is betting on its own sovereignty at the moment when the infrastructures of that future—compute, cloud, models, energy, land—are being built elsewhere and rented back to us. The day's three sessions take each question

title: Strategic Autonomy — Quantum Science and the New Non-Alignment
description: Quantum is where European scientific strength and European industrial dependency meet most sharply: the research base is world-class, the supply chains, capital and manufacturing are not. Tommaso Calarco, one of the architects of Europe’s quantum research programme, and Martin Rauchbauer, Austria’s first tech ambassador to Silicon Valley and founder of the Tech Diplomacy Network, ask whether Europe can act as a non-aligned power between the blocs—and what a science, arts and technology diplomacy

title: Epic Fury: The Dark Art of Defense Tech
description: Defence technology has acquired an aesthetic—sleek, heroic, unmistakably neo-Futurist—and that aesthetic does political work. Simon Denny, who has spent a decade taking apart the visual languages of extraction, crypto and corporate power, turns to Palantir, Anduril and their European imitators: how militarised AI is made to look both inevitable and desirable, who is flattered by that imagery and what it keeps out of frame.

title: The Authoritarian Stack
description: Francesca Bria traces the rise of the authoritarian tech right in Silicon Valley and the alignment now consolidating around it: reactionary ideology, venture capital, defence and government contracts and private platforms that have quietly become state infrastructure—cloud, identity, policing, borders. She calls it the Authoritarian Stack and argues that Europe cannot regulate its way out of a dependency it has already accepted. What it needs is an industrial strategy for democratic infrastructu

title: Mechanical Kurds
description: Hito Steyerl, Professor of Emergent Digital Media at the Academy of Fine Arts Munich, won the STARTS Prize ’26 Grand Prize for Artistic Exploration with Mechanical Kurds. The title recalls the eighteenth-century automaton that appeared to play chess by itself while concealing a human operator, and the Amazon platform that later borrowed the name. In Erbil, Kurdish-Syrian refugees label military imagery through crowdsourcing platforms without knowing what it serves. The performance-lecture follow

title: Soul or Arsenal?
description: European autonomy can turn in two directions: a public digital commons, or a militarised arsenal built with public money and held in private hands. The morning’s three speakers take the choice head-on, bringing together its political economy, its aesthetics and its geopolitics, and put the practical question to the room: which institutions, investments, imaginaries and alliances would make the first outcome real, and how much time is left to build them.

title: The Data Workers’ Inquiry: In Their Own Words
description: AI systems rest on work that is deliberately kept out of view: labelling images, filtering violent content, correcting and rating outputs—outsourced to the Global South and precarious almost everywhere. Julia Kloiber speaks with Victoria De Napoli, writer, musician and researcher, part of the Data Workers’ Inquiry, who worked as a trainer for a technology company building AI systems and is making a documentary about it. What the work does to the people who do it, and what rights, dignity and org

title: Eccentric Engineering: Building Otherwise
description: Tega Brain is an artist and environmental engineer who builds working systems rather than critiques: Solar Protocol, a network of volunteer-run solar servers where the sun decides which one serves the internet; Asunder, a fictional artificial environmental manager that proposes what to sacrifice to keep the planet within its limits; tools for refusing and obscuring personal data. Her keynote makes the case for eccentric engineering based on minimal computing, good-enough prediction, infrastructu

title: What Alternatives? Power, Labour, Planet
description: From diagnosis to alternatives. Data centres are arriving in European regions faster than grids, water systems and planning authorities can absorb them and the public is rarely asked. This conversation brings together the researchers, campaigners and builders working on the material footprint of AI and on what could be built instead: public and cooperative infrastructure, ecological limits treated as design constraints, global public goods and computing within humanity’s limits rather than beyon

title: The Architecture of Public Truth
description: Forensic Architecture built a new evidentiary practice, using architecture, modelling and open-source material to hold states and corporations to account where courts and media could not. Eyal Weizman extends the method to the planet itself: the earth as a forensic object that registers pollution, ruin, environmental violence and genocide. The keynote asks what institutions such evidence demands if it is to count, and who is entitled to produce public truth.

title: Children of a Modest Star: Governing Beyond the Nation-State
description: Planetary problems, national institutions: the mismatch defines the century. Nils Gilman, co-author of Children of a Modest Star, argues that neither a world government nor the nation-state as we have it can govern climate, pandemics or computation and makes the case for multi-scale institutions built to the shape of the problems themselves—a form of planetary politics that does not wait for consensus between states.

title: The More-than-Human Laboratory
description: Agnes Meyer-Brandis won the STARTS Prize ’26 Grand Prize for Innovative Collaboration with the Office for Tree Migration, a long-term project following how trees and plants move as climate zones shift: north, uphill into the Californian White Mountains, into the peatlands. Her work sits between scientific research, fieldwork and myth, building experiments that are at once rigorous and wayward. The talk explores what it would mean to observe, shape and develop from a position that is not exclusiv

title: Antimonuments
description: For three decades Rafael Lozano-Hemmer has built participatory installations that turn public space into sites of encounter and turn surveillance technology against itself: searchlights over Mexico City’s Zócalo steered by participants online; shadows twenty metres high filled with the portraits of passers-by; rooms that pulse with the recorded heartbeats of everyone who has entered them; biometric systems put to work searching for the disappeared; bridges of light opening live voice channels ac

title: Closing—Coexistence and Possible Futures
description: The day closes on the question it opened with: what did we negotiate and which futures now feel possible? A short reflection on coexistence across geographical and geopolitical blocs and across the divide between those who build these systems and those who carry their cost—and on what the day leaves to be built as planetary alternatives for humanity.

title: Leonardo LASER Talks Linz – Lab Songs Vol. III: Stardust Paella
description:
Leonardo LASER is an international program that brings together artists, scientists, academics and the public to share their work and inspire one another through presentations, performances and discussions.

description:
Leonardo LASER is an international program that brings together artists, scientists, academics, and the public to share their work and inspire one another through presentations, performances and discussions.

Our recurring LASER series, Lab Songs, explores evolving cultures of experimentation. Scientific and artistic breakthroughs arise not only from discoveries, but from transformations in practices, methodologies and systems of care. As a result, laboratories are increasingly reimagined as spa

title: Negotiating Humanity
description:
This exhibition presents six works—primarily Golden Nica and Grand Prize winners— selected from the Prix Ars Electronica 2026 (4,329 submissions from 106 countries) and the European Commission’s STARTS Prize 2026 (2,719 submissions from 110 countries).

Each of these works deconstructs and reimagines, with striking necessity, the notion of “humanity” that we have long taken for granted—from diverse perspectives, including bodily perception, the nature of capitalist technology, the new autonomous

title: FESTIVAL WALK: Negotiating the Real
description: What we see, hear and feel, we interpret as reality. It appears immediate, yet it is already filtered, ordered and interpreted. title: What we can hear and cannot understand
description: Posthuman Radio: What we can hear and cannot understand is a live sonic cabaret. The set is a makeshift radio studio run on XR-as-Stage principles, a writeable room where realities are rehearsed as much as recorded and anyone in it can change the score. Artists, scientists, performers, AI agents, humans and non-humans share the bill, and conversations, field recordings and sonic art run at once. A radio play—and we take play as seriously as an experiment. Tune in.

title: Being in Relationship with Water
description: Through the lens of Indigenous ontologies, Craft will explore what is it to be in relationships of responsibility to water. Using the Decolonizing Water project—an Indigenous-led partnership committed to revitalizing Indigenous water governance—as a starting point, Craft talks about the community-led research conducted by the initiative and the importance of understanding lands and water not only as sites of learning, but also as being actively involved in the process of education.

title: Policy Lab “The Empty Chair”
description: The policy lab asks: What becomes possible when Upper Austria connects industry, technology and research with media arts and creative industries? Which alliances, structures and future skills would this require? Around 20 people from policy, industry, technology, research and creative practice meet at one table. An empty chair marks a strategic role still vacant. Košice shares lessons on linking creative talent with technology, business and public institutions.
